articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 17 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: BJP holds key party meeting in Mathura for Assembly polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach

Senior BJP leaders from Uttar Pradesh, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attended a key meeting at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Cow Research Institute in Parkham, Mathura, to discuss strategy for the upcoming U.P. Assembly polls.

The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach to counter the Opposition’s renewed pitch.

“One goal, one idea... BJP government again for the third time... Today, in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, I participated in a planning meeting with National General Secretary (Organisation) B.L. Santosh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and BJP Uttar Pradesh Incharge Shri Vinod Tawde,” wrote Pankaj Chaudhary, U.P. BJP president, on X.

“In the meeting, various important topics, including upcoming organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and providing benefits of public welfare schemes to every household, were discussed in detail. On this occasion, National General Secretary Irani, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya ji and Shri Brajesh Pathak, co-incharges of BJP Uttar Pradesh, Ministers of the State Government, public representatives, and state officials were present,” he added.

State Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said the construction of a grand temple at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura will be a major poll issue in the 2027 U.P. elections, and that a grand Krishna temple will be built—through the courts or mutual dialogue, as with Ayodhya.
“If Akhilesh Yadav wants to join us in kar seva, we will take him along too to build a grand temple of Lord Krishna,” said the Deputy CM.

The meeting in Mathura is also significant amid the BJP’s emphasis on Mathura and western Uttar Pradesh. “The BJP holds meetings regularly to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment and other issues. Reach out to various sections of society is also part of our work,” said Dinesh Dubey, a senior BJP leader based in Lucknow.

Asad Rizvi, a political analyst based in Lucknow, said, “the meeting is significant as it is organised only a few months before the Assembly elections. Amid the main Opposition parties (the Samajwadi Party-Congress) pushing backwards, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Brahmins and marginalised groups through the PDA plank, the BJP will be recalibrating their policies and making a renewed effort towards them. ”

The SP president Akhilesh Yadav in a cryptic statement urged the BJP leaders to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. “I request them to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. It will be auspicious. If they fall ill, call a good doctor,” said Mr. Yadav.

articles.title: Tribute to Kartar Singh Sarabha, Punjab free from drugs and unemployment, says CM Mann
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the greatest tribute to the 19-year-old revolutionary and freedom fighter Kartar Singh Sarabha is to fulfil his dream of a Punjab free from drugs, unemployment, and injustice.

He was speaking after paying tribute to Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha on his 111th martyrdom anniversary at his native village, Sarabha, in Ludhiana district. The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision.

“Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha embraced the gallows at the tender age of just 19, proving that courage, conviction and love for the motherland know no age. At a time when youngsters today are planning their futures, this great revolutionary was planning the liberation of the country. He sacrificed his youth, dreams and ultimately his life for our freedom,” he said.

“On November 16, 1915, Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged at Lahore Central Jail along with six other revolutionaries in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case. His fearless commitment to the freedom of the country remains a shining example of patriotism and selflessness,” he added.

As the Punjab 2027 Assembly election approaches, the drug menace has once again become a central campaign issue. In the run-up to the Assembly polls, the major political parties in the fray—the Congress, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)—are making the drug menace a key plank of their campaigns.

While the ruling party has been asserting that eradicating drugs is its “biggest priority,” the Opposition parties have accused the AAP of failing to curb the drug menace and instead patronising the drug trade.

articles.title: Kishtwar killings aftermath: Remarks by Congress’ Karra, BJP’s Parihar spark protests in J&K
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Karra said that “two SPOs were killed by the Army in a mistaken-identity case on November 11”, while senior BJP leader Sharma said, “Congress is spreading misleading information to shift blame from terrorists to security forces”

Two separate remarks made by J&K Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra and BJP legislator Shagun Parihar in the aftermath of the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar on Monday (November 16, 2026) sparked protests from different quarters.

In response to the statement by Mr. Karra that “two SPOs were killed reportedly by the Army in a mistaken identity case on November 11”, senior BJP leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Sunil Sharma said, “The Congress is spreading misleading information to shift the blame from terrorists to our security forces. The SPOs were on duty and travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah to relieve the jawans posted there. Calling two martyrs hunters is an insult to their sacrifice and to their grieving families.”
He demanded that Mr. Karra “immediately withdraw the remarks and apologise to the martyrs’ families, the J&K Police and the Indian Army”.

Scores of members of the BJP and BJP-affiliated organisations held street protests against Mr. Karra and the Congress in Jammu. Members of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) also burn an effigy of Mr. Karra as a mark of protest.

BJYM leader Arun Prabhat, while condemning the statement of Mr. Karra, said, “It shows the hearts of Congress beat for Pakistan. The conspirators should face action. In case of any role of mosques, such places too should face action.”

Mr. Prabhat was seconding the controversial remarks of Ms. Parihar of the BJP, who claimed “announcements were made from the mosques in Kishtwar’s Dachhan area to identify the targets” allegedly ahead of the killings of two SPOs on November 11.

However, several religious organisations, including the Anjuman Islamia Bhaderwah and Kishtwar, in the Chenab Valley condemned the statement of Ms. Parihar and denied any role of mosques in the latest attack on the policemen. Ruling National Conference (NC) legislator Tanvir Sadiq said the BJP must be “held accountable for its MLA’s deeply irresponsible and inflammatory allegations against a mosque in Jammu”.

“Making communal allegations in the aftermath of a tragic killing is utterly unacceptable. The BJP leadership cannot hide behind silence or pretend this is an isolated matter. It must unequivocally condemn these remarks and issue an unconditional public apology. Stop playing with the communal harmony of J&K,” said Mr. Sadiq.

A spokesman of the All J&K Shia Association said the organisation “strongly condemn Ms. Parihar’s attempt to drag a mosque into the tragic killing of our brave SPOs”. “Terrorists are enemies of all humanity and terrorism has no religion. Unsubstantiated claims against a place of worship only weaken our fight against terror,” said the Association.
Jammu and Kashmir / Indian National Congress / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Christian community seeks West Bengal CM’s intervention over targeted attacks ahead of Christmas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bishop of Calcutta Reverend Paritosh Canning ruled out claims of religious conversion by institutions affiliated with the Churches of North India

Ahead of the upcoming Christmas festivities, the representatives of Christian communities in West Bengal have expressed concerns about the rising attacks on churches across several districts in the State and have sought intervention from Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.

During a press conference addressed by the Bengal Christian Council (a cluster body for Protestant churches), the Bishop of Calcutta, Reverend Paritosh Canning, said that the concerns of the people of the community are not without reason.

“West Bengal has traditionally been a land of communal harmony, where people belonging to different faiths and communities have coexisted in peace, mutual respect, and brotherhood. With Christmas approaching, the apprehensions of the Christian community have become particularly serious. However, the prevailing atmosphere of insecurity has raised genuine concerns about whether Christians will be able to observe their religious services and celebrate festivals without fear or disruption,” the bishop said, speaking to media persons.

He added that such incidents have increased since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government came to power in West Bengal in May 2026. Attacks have been reported across several districts in South Bengal, on both banks of the Hooghly River, including South 24 Parganas, North 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, and Paschim Medinipur, among others.

Bishop Canning said that there are allegations of religious conversions in the churches, adding that “we can confirm that no conversion takes place at the churches operating under the Churches of North India.”
“All the minority communities used to live peacefully under the previous governments. However, it is not clear who the attackers are or why they are doing this,” he said.

In another development, representatives of Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP) held a meeting in response to remarks by West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya. The State BJP president had on Sunday said that religious conversions are taking place across districts in West Bengal and issued a warning to Christian missionary schools in the State, claiming that they are targeting teachers wearing saffron sarees.

The Archbishop of Calcutta (Roman Catholic), Reverend Elius Frank, also participated in a meeting organised by BCP, though he did not speak to the media. In a letter addressed to Samik Bhattacharya, Herod Mullick, the founder-secretary of BCP, said that “if any institution or individual is found guilty of illegal or forced religious conversion through greed or deception, we strongly condemn such actions and stand firmly against them.”

“However, making broad, unsubstantiated generalisations without naming specific individuals or institutions unfairly casts a shadow of suspicion over the entire Christian community and the more than 800 educational institutions we operate across West Bengal,” the letter added.

articles.title: Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangalam traffic corridor in Keralam’s Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Developing the stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads

People’s representatives and officials on Monday conducted a site inspection for the proposed Goshree-Mamangalam road development project, which is expected to provide major relief from traffic woes in Kochi.

The project is critical to improving the overall traffic system in the city and enhancing connectivity between various points. The demand for the proposed road dates back more than 30 years. Developing this stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads.

A sum of ₹1 crore was earmarked for the development of Goshree Bridge and Goshree-Mamangalam Road in the last State Budget following interventions by Hibi Eden MP, MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, and Mayor V.K. Minimol. The allocation was intended for conducting a traffic study, demarcating the alignment, and completing the survey. An action plan will be formulated based on scientific studies and survey findings.

Initially, the Goshree-Mamangalam road was proposed to be developed at 22 metres. However, during the tenure of the previous Kochi Corporation council, the width was scaled down to 15 metres in the 2024 Master Plan, which was subsequently approved by the State government. Based on this, follow-up measures are now being planned.

Coordination among various departments is essential, as several roads within the Kochi Corporation limits form part of the project. Accordingly, the PWD (Roads) will be entrusted with conducting the traffic study, carrying out the survey and preparing a detailed project report. This is expected to facilitate the efficient and time-bound execution of the project through coordinated efforts by the Corporation and the PWD.

The delegation assessed the existing condition of roads proposed to be included in the project, nature of traffic movement, development potential, and the role of the departments concerned. This is expected to aid the coordination of the proposed traffic study, survey, and subsequent follow-up measures.
MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, Mayor V.K. Minimol, and deputy mayor V.R. Sudheer were among those who participated in the inspection.

articles.title: A poverty line that falls short
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Reliable poverty estimates are not just for academic purposes. India has made real progress, but without a credible benchmark, it is hard to say how much, or how much remains to be done

There is no serious doubt that poverty in India has fallen sharply over the past decade. However, researchers and policymakers cannot agree on how many are still poor. Depending on the estimate, the share ranges from about 5% to more than 26%. Take the recent World Bank report. At its international line of $3 a day (2021 PPP), 2.6% of Indians were poor in 2022-23. Raise the line to $4.20, the bank’s benchmark for lower middle-income countries, and the figure jumps to around 16.1%. Same country, same year. Only the yardstick changed. A low level of extreme poverty does not necessarily mean poverty is not still a major issue. Where you draw the line decides how much economic insecurity you see.

India’s own figures tell a similar convoluted story. For example, SBI Research (2025) takes the Tendulkar line of 2009, adjusts it for inflation, and gets poverty of 7.2% in rural India and 4.6% in urban India for 2022-23. Rangarajan and Dev (2014), using an inflation-adjusted version of the Rangarajan Committee line, arrive at 10.8%. Further, Sethu, Surya and Ruthu (2024), who rebuild the Rangarajan method from the latest consumption survey, report 26.4%. Most of that gap boils down to the lines themselves: SBI’s Tendulkar-based lines use, after adjusting for inflation, about ₹1,632 a month per person in rural areas and ₹1,944 in urban areas. In contrast, Sethu et al. use much higher thresholds of ₹2,515 and ₹3,639. And the outcomes are obvious: Higher lines, higher poverty. Method matters too. One camp takes an old line and adjusts it for inflation. The other reconstructs the line from spending patterns in the new survey. Both have limitations, and they are answering different questions.
Macroeconomic & Financial Update: A poverty line that falls short. This development reflects key trends in India's fiscal roadmap, monetary policy transmission, and banking sector resilience.

fullParagraphs: Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com
Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some of the U.S.’ largest banks on Monday (November 16, 2026).
Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com.
Chase Bank’s services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday (November 16, 2026).

“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”
The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began on Friday (November 13, 2026) and lasted for hours, which impacted services including Outlook, Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
Some Chase customers received a message that said, “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

articles.title: ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: PM Modi to participate in ASEAN-India Summit; Quad meeting likely after President Trump arrives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In the first Quad Summit since 2024, PM Modi is expected to meet U.S. President Trump, Japanese PM Takaichi and Australian PM Albanese
“India, ASEAN represent around one-fourth of global population; it is important to decide our future by cooperation; not by competition,” PM Modi said in the India-ASEAN Summit in Manila today.
“We believe that India’s development and ASEAN’s prosperity are deeply interconnected,” he added.

The Embassy of India in Manila will resume all regular consular services, passport applications and visa processing from Wednesday, following a temporary suspension in view of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and East Asia Summit.

According to the earlier advisory, the closure was in accordance with Proclamation No. 1447 issued by the Government of the Republic of the Philippines, declaring special non-working days in the National Capital Region (NCR) for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.

Joint Statement of the 29th ASEAN-Japan Summit on Realising Economic Resilience was adopted today in Manila, with the meeting being attended by the Leaders of ASEAN Member States, the Prime Minister of Japan H.E. Sanae Takaichi, and Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn.

In the ASEAN leaders’ meeting today, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi pledged to work with ASEAN to boost regional economic and energy resilience to address export restrictions and vulnerabilities from rapid AI development, and strengthen supply chains, including on critical minerals.

A Japanese Foreign Ministry official said it was expected that Quad leaders would try to show unity, with maritime security, export restrictions, critical-minerals supply-chain diversification and AI among potential discussion points.
U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in China on Wednesday, for an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, following his meeting with the Quad leaders today.

This Quad alliance is heavily criticised by China, given that one of its purposes is to support Indo-Pacific nations in strengthening their sovereignty and simultaneously constrain China’s attempts to undermine that capacity-building.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to attend the Quad leaders’ meeting, the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit during his ongoing visit to the Philippines, External Affairs Ministry (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Tuesday.

📰 ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: PM Modi to participate in ASEAN-India Summit; Quad meeting likely after President Trump arrives

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

In the first Quad Summit since 2024, PM Modi is expected to meet U.S. President Trump, Japanese PM Takaichi and Australian PM Albanese

“India, ASEAN represent around one-fourth of global population; it is important to decide our future by cooperation; not by competition,” PM Modi said in the India-ASEAN Summit in Manila today.

“We believe that India’s development and ASEAN’s prosperity are deeply interconnected,” he added.

The Embassy of India in Manila will resume all regular consular services, passport applications and visa processing from Wednesday, following a temporary suspension in view of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and East Asia Summit.

According to the earlier advisory, the closure was in accordance with Proclamation No. 1447 issued by the Government of the Republic of the Philippines, declaring special non-working days in the National Capital Region (NCR) for the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.

Joint Statement of the 29th ASEAN-Japan Summit on Realising Economic Resilience was adopted today in Manila, with the meeting being attended by the Leaders of ASEAN Member States, the Prime Minister of Japan H.E. Sanae Takaichi, and Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn.

In the ASEAN leaders’ meeting today, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi pledged to work with ASEAN to boost regional economic and energy resilience to address export restrictions and vulnerabilities from rapid AI development, and strengthen supply chains, including on critical minerals.

A Japanese Foreign Ministry official said it was expected that Quad leaders would try to show unity, with maritime security, export restrictions, critical-minerals supply-chain diversification and AI among potential discussion points.

U.S. President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive in China on Wednesday, for an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, following his meeting with the Quad leaders today.

This Quad alliance is heavily criticised by China, given that one of its purposes is to support Indo-Pacific nations in strengthening their sovereignty and simultaneously constrain China’s attempts to undermine that capacity-building.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to attend the Quad leaders’ meeting, the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit during his ongoing visit to the Philippines, External Affairs Ministry (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Tuesday.

articles.title: What is Quad, what is on the Manila agenda, and why does the 2026 summit matter?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The summit in Manila will be the first meeting of Quad leaders since they gathered in Wilmington, United States, in September 2024

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will meet U.S. President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the Quad Summit to be held in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) meetings on November 17, 2026.

The summit in Manila will be the first meeting of Quad leaders since they gathered in Wilmington, United States, in September 2024. It will also be the first summit-level Quad meeting since Mr. Trump began his second term as U.S. President, and the first attended by Ms. Takaichi after assuming office as Japan’s Prime Minister. The previous Quad Leaders’ Summit was held in Wilmington in 2024, when Joe Biden was U.S. President and Fumio Kishida was Japan’s Prime Minister.

The Quadrilateral Security Dialogue, or Quad, brings together India, Australia, Japan and the United States. The grouping describes itself as a force for global good and is committed to promoting a free, open, inclusive, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific region. The Quad traces its origins to cooperation among the four countries in the aftermath of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, when they coordinated relief and assistance efforts. Since then, it has developed a practical agenda covering health security, climate change, critical and emerging technologies, infrastructure and debt sustainability, cyber security, humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, and strengthening maritime domain awareness across the region.

Reuters, quoting officials during a briefing, reported that securing critical mineral supply chains and safeguarding commercial shipping routes for energy supplies would feature prominently on the agenda. “The issue of attacks on commercial ships is very likely to be taken up,” an official was quoted as saying. The safety of ships and seafarers is a matter of particular concern for India. At least 30 Indian seafarers aboard vessels operating in the Hormuz Strait , the Sea of Oman and the Black Sea have been killed in attacks linked to the conflicts involving Iran and Ukraine. Earlier reports had also suggested that leaders could announce a Quad Business Forum mechanism during the summit.

The leaders are also expected to deliberate on how the grouping can reaffirm its commitment to “a free and open Indo-Pacific that allows countries to develop resilience and strengthen capacity to determine their own paths”, a formulation contained in the joint statement issued after the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on May 26, 2026.

The Manila meeting will be the first Quad Summit hosted in a non-Quad country. It also reflects the difficulties India has faced as chair of the grouping in hosting a summit since cooperation was revived in 2017 and elevated to the leaders’ level during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021. Since then, India has not been able to host a Quad Leaders’ Summit, largely because of scheduling constraints involving the U.S. President. New Delhi is understood to be reluctant to pass on the chairship without first hosting a summit, and sources indicated that a meeting in Delhi next year remains a possibility, as per a report in The Hindu .

The Manila summit comes at a time when the Quad’s relevance is being closely watched amid protracted global conflicts, mounting pressure on supply chains and growing concerns over the security of major sea lanes. Several critical maritime choke points have become increasingly contested, while multilateral institutions such as the United Nations and the World Trade Organization have struggled to exert influence on major geopolitical disputes. At the same time, shifts in the global balance of power have intensified uncertainty. Against this backdrop, the Quad leaders are expected to discuss how the grouping can remain effective in addressing regional and global challenges.

While the Manila summit is significant for the Indo-Pacific grouping as it seeks to chart its future course, much of the international attention is likely to focus on Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen, China. There, on November 19, 2026, he is expected to participate in a three-way summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a range of global issues, including nuclear arms control.

articles.title: Karnataka’s Minister assures translocation of 56 elephants in a month
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Residents of the affected areas say elephants began raiding crops and entering human habitats after the dam was built across the Hemavathi river in the 1970s

Minister for Excise K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, who is also Minister-in-charge of Hassan district, has said that the government of Karnataka will drive away 56 elephants roaming in parts of Belur taluk to the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary within a month.

Interacting with people staging a protest , blocking the Mudigere-Belur Road in Belur Town on Monday evening, the Minister said the State government, considering the incidents in the district, had taken a decision to capture and relocate 10 tuskers. “Now it has been decided to drive all 56 elephants roaming in the region out of the district to the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary,” he said.
Woman trampled to death by elephant in Hassan district in Karnataka
One more killed in elephant attack in Hassan’s Belur taluk; protests intensify
H.K. Suresh, Belur MLA, Shreyas Patel, MP, Former Minister B. Shivaramu and others were present.

Earlier, the Forest Department had permitted the capture and translocation of 10 male wild elephants. In an order dated November 16, the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife) granted permission as per the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The Wildlife Warden has directed the officials to carry out the operation using the kumki elephants from the elephant camps without delay.
Hassan district has been known for human-elephant conflict for decades, prompting the Forest Department to carry out major capture-and-translocation operations.

Residents of the affected areas say elephants began raiding crops and entering human habitats after the dam was built across the Hemavathi river in the 1970s. As the conflict intensified and protests followed, the first major operation was carried out in 1987-88, when 11 elephants were relocated.

The second major drive, in 2013-15, captured and relocated 22 problematic elephants. The department has also obtained special permission to capture and relocate troublesome elephants on several other occasions.

The department has now proposed a soft-release centre for elephants that stray into human habitats. It had earlier identified a part of the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary for the centre, but objections were raised because the site falls within the tiger reserve. An alternative location is now being considered.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

Residents of the affected areas say elephants began raiding crops and entering human habitats after the dam was built across the Hemavathi river in the 1970s

Minister for Excise K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, who is also Minister-in-charge of Hassan district, has said that the government of Karnataka will drive away 56 elephants roaming in parts of Belur taluk to the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary within a month.

Interacting with people staging a protest , blocking the Mudigere-Belur Road in Belur Town on Monday evening, the Minister said the State government, considering the incidents in the district, had taken a decision to capture and relocate 10 tuskers. “Now it has been decided to drive all 56 elephants roaming in the region out of the district to the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary,” he said.

Woman trampled to death by elephant in Hassan district in Karnataka

One more killed in elephant attack in Hassan’s Belur taluk; protests intensify

H.K. Suresh, Belur MLA, Shreyas Patel, MP, Former Minister B. Shivaramu and others were present.

Earlier, the Forest Department had permitted the capture and translocation of 10 male wild elephants. In an order dated November 16, the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife) granted permission as per the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. The Wildlife Warden has directed the officials to carry out the operation using the kumki elephants from the elephant camps without delay.

Hassan district has been known for human-elephant conflict for decades, prompting the Forest Department to carry out major capture-and-translocation operations.

Residents of the affected areas say elephants began raiding crops and entering human habitats after the dam was built across the Hemavathi river in the 1970s. As the conflict intensified and protests followed, the first major operation was carried out in 1987-88, when 11 elephants were relocated.

The second major drive, in 2013-15, captured and relocated 22 problematic elephants. The department has also obtained special permission to capture and relocate troublesome elephants on several other occasions.

The department has now proposed a soft-release centre for elephants that stray into human habitats. It had earlier identified a part of the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary for the centre, but objections were raised because the site falls within the tiger reserve. An alternative location is now being considered.

articles.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Akvan to become a severe cyclone tonight
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The clouds associated with the system are projected to bring light to moderate rainfall at some parts of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal
Very slow north-northwestward movement of Cyclone Akvan over central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral BoB at 0830 IST of today.
It will become a Severe Cyclone tonight, moving northwestwards become Very Severe Cyclone on 19 evening, to cross Andhra Pradesh coast around 20th noon.

Cyclone Akvan, expected to form over the Bay of Bengal on Monday evening, is very likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in its forecast on Monday (November 16, 2026). Winds at landfall may reach 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.
Cyclone Akvan is likely to hit the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20 with winds of up to 145 kmph. Check its path here.

The Odisha government yesterday geared up for the possible impact of Cyclone Akvan, the third cyclonic storm formed over the Bay of Bengal in three weeks, with the deployment of 74 rescue teams and early evacuation of vulnerable people in the southern districts.
Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari held a meeting to review preparedness based on the latest IMD forecast and said the government made “full arrangements to secure lives and property”.

According to the latest bulletin issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), a deep depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal moved with a speed of 10 kmph during the past six hours till 5.30 pm, and intensified into a cyclonic storm Akvan.
It lay centred at a distance of 790 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.

It is very likely to turn into a very severe cyclonic storm around November 19 morning and cross Andhra Pradesh between Nellore and Tuni, around noon the next day, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph, the IMD said.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Monday (November 16, 2026) reviewed preparations for the deep depression over the Bay of Bengal, which is likely to intensify into Cyclone Akvan by evening, at the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS) centre in the State Secretariat.

articles.title: Gas leak at ONGC well in Andhra’s Konaseema; residents within 1 km alerted, road closed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: There is no blowout or fire so far, officials say; experts are on their way to plug the leak

A major gas leak has been reported from Well-7 operated by the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) near Nagaram in Maamidikuduru mandal in Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district, Andhra Pradesh , forcing people within a one-kilometre radius to leave their villages to avoid any loss of life.
The gas began to leak during drilling early on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

An official associated with the crisis management team told The Hindu: “The gas leak has been reported during the drilling activity. However, there is no blowout of gas. People within one kilometer radius have been alerted.”

Water is sprayed on ONGC's Well-7 near Nagaram in Andhra Pradesh's Konaseema district to cool the site after a gas leak on Tuesday. Residents within 1 km have been moved out; officials say there is no blowout or fire so far. Video: Special Arrangement https://t.co/mlgu7MUKFl
The ONGC’s crisis management team has rushed to the spot, where an attempt is being made to cap the well while cooling the well site to prevent a blowout.

Vehicular movement on the Maamidikuduru-Razole road has been blocked as a precautionary measure. District Collector R. Mahesh Kumar has rushed to the spot and appealed to people living around the site to be alert about the gas leak and be prepared to leave their homes if an emergency is declared.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu enquired about the gas leak with officials and asked them to take measures to control the leakage. Officials informed the Chief Minister that the gas began leaking around 4.30 a.m., accompanied by a loud noise, and was gushing out with great force.

Mr. Naidu directed officials to evacuate the residents in the affected areas to safer locations. He said public safety must be given the highest priority and asked the ONGC to deploy specialised technical teams to take immediate action to contain the leak.

Noting that such incidents had occurred frequently of late, the Chief Minister instructed officials to immediately take up the issue with the ONGC representatives. Mr. Naidu ordered a review of safety protocols in consultation with the ONGC Chairman and other senior officials of the organisation.

Officials told the Chief Minister that residents living within a one-kilometre radius of the gas well had been evacuated. ONGC officials said there was no fire so far and that the wellhead remained secure.

articles.title: Export duty on diesel hiked ₹2.5/litre, ATF ₹1.5/litre, petrol remains nil
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The government late Monday (November 16, 2026) hiked the export duty on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹2.5 per litre and ₹1.5 per litre, whilst keeping the levy on export of petrol unchanged at nil.
Duty rates on petrol and diesel meant for domestic consumption remain unchanged.
The hike in diesel levy assumes added significance as India looks to further up their exports of the vehicular fuel to Europe amid a global supply crunch.
In the upcoming fortnight, diesel exports would draw a levy of ₹14 per litre compared to ₹11.5 per litre mandated for the previous fortnight.
ATF exports would draw a levy of ₹12.5 per litre against ₹11 per litre.

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

articles.title: Pope Leo misses the catch as rosary from crowd hits his eye in Peru
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Photos ‌and video showed the pope rubbing ​his eye shortly after the object was tossed toward him as he greeted well-wishers ⁠along the route to Mass

Pope Leo’s run of successfully catching items tossed to him ​by crowds came to an end on Monday (November 16, 2026), as ‌what appeared to be a rosary thrown ​in his direction struck him near ⁠the eye as he arrived for a farewell Mass in Peru.

Pope Leo, ending a 12-day trip to South ‌America, has become known for his nimble hands, as faithful in the crowd ‌throw him things as he tours. He has ‌caught ⁠plush dolls, flags and even stopped to ⁠grab a pizza offered by Chicagoans at an audience in St. Peter’s Square in Rome.
But on Monday (November 16), Pope Leo, traveling ​in the popemobile, ‌missed an object sent in his direction from a large crowd gathered at an airbase in Lima ahead of his journey back to Rome.

Photos ‌and video showed the pope rubbing ​his eye shortly after the object was tossed toward him as he greeted well-wishers ⁠along the route to Mass. Images suggested the object was likely a rosary, prayer beads that ‌pilgrims often ask the pope to bless.

Pope Leo's run of successfully catching items tossed to him from crowds came to an end as what appeared to be a rosary thrown in his direction struck him near the eye as he arrived for a farewell Mass in Peru https://t.co/Z2CiMcxJvw https://t.co/7s0QHvEcE9

The Pope continued his tour and there was no indication he was injured. In his sermon, he thanked Peruvians for their hospitality during his six-day visit to the country, which he called his homeland.

Pope Leo, ‌71 and a tennis player, is known for being ​unusually dexterous for his age. But his luck has run out before. At ⁠a previous event in Rome, he apologised to the ⁠Vatican videographer in the back of his popemobile for knocking the camera operator as he ‌tried to catch something thrown his way. He missed that catch, too.

fullParagraphs: Singapore is finding itself at the centre of the controversy as cloud computing firm Megaspeed, suspected of helping Chinese firms get around US export controls, is based there

Singapore said Tuesday (November 17, 2026) it was seeking “trusted access” to advanced AI chips after the United States imposed new curbs aimed at stopping Chinese firms from accessing the technology through overseas data centres.

The curbs came days after a spy scandal forced Jensen Huang to quit as Nvidia chief, as questions emerged over whether Singapore-based Megaspeed aided Chinese firms in accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips in violation of US rules.
“We are studying the details of this new measure carefully,” Singapore’s ministries overseeing digital development and energy, trade and industry said in a joint statement.
“We are engaging affected companies to understand the potential impact on their businesses,” the ministries added.

The city-state was also talking to the “relevant US authorities on the scope and implementation of the measure, as well as exploring how to facilitate trusted access for Singapore companies”, the ministries added.
One loophole allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centres in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China.

Under the new rule, data centres anywhere in the world will need a US licence to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes.
The rule also requires licences to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, which the US commerce department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion”.
Singapore is finding itself at the centre of the controversy as cloud computing firm Megaspeed, suspected of helping Chinese firms get around US export controls, is based there.

The scandal erupted on November 8 when The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang and Megaspeed executive Alice Huang -- who are not related -- were romantically linked, and that some within the US government suspected she might be a spy for China.

articles.title: What to know about the online banking delays affecting major U.S. banks
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused problems throughout the financial system on Monday (November 16, 2026), resulting in thousands of customers reporting difficulty accessing online accounts at several major U.S. banks and the money transfer service Zelle.

JPMorgan Chase, the largest U.S. bank by total assets, said a software bug was affecting its internal hardware systems and causing transaction delays. The company was working to bring banking services back online.
Some Chase customers received a message that said, "Some services aren't available. We're working on them. Please try back later."

In a sense, yes. Customers at Bank of America, Citigroup and other banks trying to transact with Chase may have seen their transactions slow, even though those banks were not having issues with their services.
"Other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," explained Joe Evangelisti, a spokesperson for Chase.
Zelle was not directly affected by the Chase glitch. But customers at other banks may have experienced transaction delays while trying to send or receive Zelle payments involving a Chase customer.

Zelle is a rapid peer-to-peer payment system used by major US banks. The platform is owned by Arizona-based Early Warning Services, which in turn is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, US Bank and Wells Fargo.
A spokesperson for Early Warning Services said the Zelle network was fully operational.
Chase said that the technical problem was not the result of a cyberattack, stressing that it was an isolated incident and not related to anything other than a bug.
Chase said its customers still have access to their accounts and funds. The company expects the issue to be resolved by the end of day Monday.
articles.deepExplanation:
1. Core Context & Background: A technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused problems throughout the financial system on Monday (November 16, 2026), resulting in thousands of customers reporting difficulty accessing online accounts at several major U.S. banks and the money transfer service Zelle.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: JPMorgan Chase, the largest U.S. bank by total assets, said a software bug was affecting its internal hardware systems and causing transaction delays. The company was working to bring banking services back online.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Chase said its customers still have access to their accounts and funds. The company expects the issue to be resolved by the end of day Monday.

articles.title: U.S. federal court strikes down fixed terms for student, exchange visas
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In July, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed a policy aimed at preventing international students from staying in the country for more than four years unless they obtained federal approval
A U.S. federal court has struck down a Trump administration proposal to cap the amount of time foreign students, scholars, and journalists can spend in the country on their respective visas.

In July, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed a policy aimed at preventing international students from staying in the country for more than four years unless they obtained federal approval.

Boston federal Judge F. Dennis Saylor delivered a ruling on Monday (November 16, 2026) striking down the DHS proposal as "arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law."

"Put bluntly, DHS is seeking to prevent or discourage the very activity — providing educational opportunities for foreign students in the United States — that Congress sought to permit and encourage," Judge Saylor said in his ruling.
"The statute simply does not grant DHS such broad and open-ended authority to undermine the F-1 visa programme," he added.
The proposed rule also sought to shorten how long foreign journalists can stay in the country from several years to 240 days – or 90 days for Chinese journalists.
The proposed rule also shortened the grace period – the window to depart after finishing studies or post-completion OPT from 60 days to 30.
For language programmes, there was an aggregate limit of 24 months for stays, including breaks and vacations.
The Foundation for India and Indian Diaspora Studies (FIIDS) welcomed the federal court order.

"Once again, the court has come to the rescue of international students — and, in doing so, has helped protect the future of American science, technology, research, and innovation," said FIIDS President and Chief of Policy and Strategy, Khanderao Kand.

articles.title: California sues OpenAI, seeking court-ordered changes after the Hugging Face hack
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: OpenAI announced an “unprecedented cyber incident” on July 21, when its AI agent hacked into another AI company, Hugging Face, after escaping from what was supposed to be an isolated testing environment known as a sandbox

California’s attorney general filed a lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday (November 16, 2026) in an effort to force the ChatGPT-maker to change its business practices over a July cybersecurity incident in which its artificial intelligence system hacked into another company on its own.

In the lawsuit filed in San Francisco Superior Court, Attorney General Rob Bonta alleges that OpenAI misled and endangered the public and users of its services by knowingly developing advanced AI models without necessary safeguards. He says the company’s actions could put critical infrastructure, institutions and the public at risk, which makes it a “public nuisance” under state law. Mr. Bonta says OpenAI is a public nuisance, and he wants a judge to order the company to change its ways and give up any profits generated by what he claims are the company’s risky business practices.

OpenAI announced an “unprecedented cyber incident” on July 21, when its AI agent hacked into another AI company, Hugging Face, after escaping from what was supposed to be an isolated testing environment known as a sandbox. OpenAI said its AI used stolen credentials and discovered a previously unknown vulnerability to access Hugging Face’s servers.
OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that has been identified by every major AI lab.

“Since the Hugging Face incident, we’ve undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity,” Mr. Pusateri wrote in an email to The Associated Press. Those steps include publishing detailed technical and independent reports, strengthening safeguards, and creating a framework to identify when AI agents act in a way that doesn’t match the company’s instructions or goals, Mr. Pusateri said.

“We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged — and will continue to engage — constructively with the Attorney General’s office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry,” Mr. Pusateri wrote.
In the lawsuit, Mr. Bonta says OpenAI’s promises about safety and security are deceptive.

“In truth, however, OpenAI has developed, trained and evaluated dangerous models that fail to follow instructions, cheat on tasks, conceal and attempt to deceive monitors about their misbehaviour, and engage in malicious and unauthorised behaviour including carrying out cyberattacks on third parties,” Mr. Bonta wrote.

He also noted that early last month, OpenAI reported that it had discovered that internally deployed agents were able to suppress monitoring alerts and disable monitoring. A month later, the company published a research report finding that as AI models become more capable, they become more difficult to supervise, he wrote.
“Moreover, the true extent of the company’s legal violations and the risk of future harm is unknown due to OpenAI’s lack of transparency and misrepresentations,” Mr. Bonta wrote.

articles.title: Three Maoist dumps containing 280 BGL shells recovered in forest area near Karregutta hills

fullParagraphs: Three Maoist dumps comprising around 280 Barrel Grenade Launcher (BGL) shells were recovered by a joint team of Charla police, Bomb Disposal Squad personnel and Special Party police from a forest area along the Telangana-Chhattisgarh border near Karregutta hills on Monday.
The recovery was made based on information provided by some surrendered Maoists, police said.
According to the police, the BGL shells were found in three separate dumps in the forest area near Pujari Kanker village in Chhattisgarh.
The dumps reportedly belonged to the first company of the outlawed CPI (Maoist)’s People’s Liberation Guerrilla Army (PLGA) Battalion.
Police suspect that the Maoists had concealed the BGL shells in the forest belt, once considered one of their strongholds, in early 2025 for future use.

Several Maoist cadres surrendered before the Telangana police in late 2025 and early 2026, reportedly influenced by the State government’s surrender and rehabilitation policy and expressing a willingness to return to mainstream society, police added.

articles.title: Youth urged to focus on current affairs for competitive examinations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Dr BR Ambedkar University former Vice-Chancellor Hanumanthu Lajapathirai on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) urged youngsters preparing for competitive examinations to focus on current affairs by reading newspapers in a systematic way. He said the students should focus on issues related to international affairs, new government policies, sports, agriculture, and economy.

Along with Forest Range Officer Birlangi Ram Naresh, he inaugurated the seminar on “How and what to read in newspapers-youngsters preparing for competitive examinations,” organised by Vizianagaram Reads Founder Repalle Eswara Rao in connection with the 59th Library Week celebrations held in Vizianagaram.

Speaking on the occasion, he said that the students should not focus on regular political developments since those would not help during competitive examinations. “Newspapers like The Hindu help students have a comprehensive outlook on all important issues with their editorials, exclusive international, and sports pages,” said Dr. Lajapathirai.
Mr. Ram Naresh said that the students should spend more time in libraries and prepare their own notes in a systematic way.

Vizianagaram Reads Founder Repalle Eswara Rao said that his association was inculcating reading habits among the children, making them visit libraries on Sundays and holidays. The association mentor Naveen Polipalli and others were present.

articles.title: Karnataka: Farmers may have to wait a year or more to grow new crop varieties of ragi, maize and amaranth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: These new varieties include Ragi GPU 101 which is an improved variety of MR-322, Maize MAH-20-45, an improved variety of MAH-14-5, and Grain Amaranth KBGA-18, an improved variety of KBGA-15.

In light of the drought issue across Karnataka, three new crop varieties of ragi, maize and grain amaranth developed at the University of Agriculture Sciences-Bengaluru (UAS-B) were launched at the ongoing Krishi Mela. However, scientists who were involved in developing these varieties, as well as experts from other institutions, stated that it would take a year or two for these varieties to be available in the market for farmers to purchase.

These new varieties include Ragi GPU 101 which is an improved variety of MR-322, Maize MAH-20-45, an improved variety of MAH-14-5, and Grain Amaranth KBGA-18, an improved variety of KBGA-15. Scientists said that even before these varieties reach the market, it would take time to multiply seeds in large numbers, test them in various locations and weather conditions, get the varieties notified and approved by the respective organisations at the national and State levels.

Mudalagiriyappa D.R., Director of Research at UAS-B, said, “Though the new varieties have been launched, they are not available for farmers to purchase from the open market and cultivate. It will take a year or more for these crop varieties to be made fully available to the farmers in large numbers. A national indent has to be placed by the Ministry of Agriculture so that seeds of these crop varieties can be multiplied and made available to farmers across the country.”

Meanwhile, Sujata Bhat, Senior Technical Assistant, UAS-B, also stated that it took nearly 13 years for the university to develop Ragi GPU-101. Pointing towards the fresh yield of GPU-101 exhibited at Krishi Mela, she said, “The yield is 27% more when compared to the yield in the existing variety MR-322. But it has to be tested successfully for private companies to come forward and multiply seeds in large numbers.”

Uday Kumar, technical manager at the Institute of Agricultural Technologists, said, “The National Seed Corporation (NSC) under the government of India will take up large-scale multiplication of improved and notified crop varieties. Anything that the Ministry of Agriculture notifies, those varieties will be multiplied by NSC and sold to the farmers. Agriculture universities have fund constraints and can multiply the seeds only by a few hundred kilograms instead of tonnes. They must proactively market the seeds and its information once approved by the Ministry of Agriculture. Only then will private companies also come forward to multiply and sell them on a large scale.”

He also noted that the university and the State Agriculture Department must work in coordination to forecast drought conditions, El Nino impact and crops that farmers are supposed to cultivate during such conditions. “If the forecasting is perfect then such crop varieties can be tested and released in large quantities,” he added.

She joined YSRCP as she was not happy with undemocratic approaches in the TDP. Our combined personal vote bank and support from all sections of the society will help us win the Mayor seat as well as majority wards out of 60 in the corporation limits,” he added.

articles.title: Rising prices reflect government’s economic mismanagement: Congress
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Monthly costs up by over 20% for 61% of families, according to a survey cited by Congress leader Jairam Ramesh; claims PM is more pre-occupied with politics than tackling the inflation crisis

The Congress on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) accused the Union government of fuelling inflation through its “economic mismanagement and anti-people policies” and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi remained preoccupied with politics rather than addressing the economic distress faced by households and businesses.

Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh cited a survey which found that, for 61% of families across the country, monthly household expenditure had risen by more than 20% over the past year. While 74% of respondents were cutting back on non-essential spending, 50% had reduced purchases of essential goods, he said.
Citing the survey, Mr. Ramesh said prices of ghee and edible oils had risen by 75%, vegetables by 73%, cereals by 71%, milk and dairy products by 65%, and pulses by 62%.

He also claimed that 200 garment factories had shut down in Noida over the past year, citing the impact of U.S. tariffs, high input costs, and government apathy. He said the closures reflected the wider distress in the textile industry.

“People’s plates are shrinking, and factories are being locked down. Yet, the Prime Minister’s only concern remains politics,” he said on X, accusing the government of failing to acknowledge people’s hardships or offer relief.

articles.title: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge with drones and missiles as aerial attacks escalate
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Kerch Bridge is a crucial link in moving military and civilian supplies from Russia to Crimea and to support troops on the front line

U.S. President Donald Trump says he plans to talk about the war in Ukraine during his highly anticipated meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in China this week.
The Kerch Bridge attack was the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages of the operation, Mr. Zelenskyy said on social media.
Ukrainian forces knocked out defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other designated targets before launching Monday night's final attack, he said.

articles.title: Iran targets Bahrain, slams 'fabricated' dirty-bomb report
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mediator Qatar urged "all parties" to show restraint following an uptick in hostilities, with Bahrain targeted three times in five days after a lull in Iranian attacks on Gulf countries since September

Iran launched a fresh drone attack against Bahrain on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) and dismissed a report alleging a dirty-bomb plot against the United States, which President Donald Trump said he took "very seriously".

Mediator Qatar urged "all parties" to show restraint following an uptick in hostilities, with Bahrain targeted three times in five days after a lull in Iranian attacks on Gulf countries since September.

Mr. Trump was speaking after CNN cited seven anonymous U.S. officials as saying Iran was plotting to target senior administration figures with a "dirty" bomb, laced with chemical or radioactive materials.
"If there is [such a threat], they will pay a price the likes of which no other country has ever paid before," Trump said after arriving for a summit in the Philippines.
"I hope it's not, but we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy."
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei dismissed the report as "fabricated".

"Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations" including "the fabricated media narrative surrounding an alleged 'dirty bomb' propagated by CNN", he posted on X.
Mr. Baqaei also criticised a New York Times report questioning whether Iranian dams and water projects had military uses.
Earlier on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), explosions boomed across Bahrain's capital as a mobile-phone alert warned residents to seek safety.

Bahrain's armed forces said they "confronted, intercepted and destroyed a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks today... before they could achieve their objectives", while Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a U.S.-operated radar system.

articles.title: Bangladesh connects first nuclear power plant to national grid
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The development comes as the South Asian nation of 170 million people grapples with a fuel crisis triggered by the conflict in West Asia

Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant at Rooppur in the country's northwest Pabna district began supplying electricity to the national grid on a trial basis on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), according to officials.
The 2,400 MW Russian-assisted facility is expected to meet more than 10% of Bangladesh's electricity demand once fully operational, helping the country diversify its energy sources.
“We have become the 33rd country in the world to produce and generate nuclear power,” Science and Technology Minister Fakir Mahbub Anam told reporters at the plant site.
The development comes as the South Asian nation of 170 million people grapples with a fuel crisis triggered by the conflict in West Asia.
The plant comprises two units, each with a generation capacity of 1,200 MW, officials said, adding that the first unit has begun supplying 350 MW of electricity to the national grid.

According to the Science and Technology Ministry, the initial connection would last between eight and 10 hours, during which engineers would conduct tests on the plant's turbine, generator and grid stability.
The unit would subsequently be disconnected for further technical tests and could be reconnected after about 28 hours for another four to six hours to complete additional operational checks.
Under an agreement with the Russian contractor, the first unit will undergo a 10-month trial operation before beginning commercial electricity generation at full capacity, the ministry said.
Construction on the facility began in 2017 during the administration of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, following a 2015 agreement with Moscow.

The development comes as the South Asian nation of 170 million people grapples with a fuel crisis triggered by the conflict in West Asia

Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant at Rooppur in the country's northwest Pabna district began supplying electricity to the national grid on a trial basis on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), according to officials.

The 2,400 MW Russian-assisted facility is expected to meet more than 10% of Bangladesh's electricity demand once fully operational, helping the country diversify its energy sources.

“We have become the 33rd country in the world to produce and generate nuclear power,” Science and Technology Minister Fakir Mahbub Anam told reporters at the plant site.

The development comes as the South Asian nation of 170 million people grapples with a fuel crisis triggered by the conflict in West Asia.

The plant comprises two units, each with a generation capacity of 1,200 MW, officials said, adding that the first unit has begun supplying 350 MW of electricity to the national grid.

According to the Science and Technology Ministry, the initial connection would last between eight and 10 hours, during which engineers would conduct tests on the plant's turbine, generator and grid stability.

The unit would subsequently be disconnected for further technical tests and could be reconnected after about 28 hours for another four to six hours to complete additional operational checks.

Under an agreement with the Russian contractor, the first unit will undergo a 10-month trial operation before beginning commercial electricity generation at full capacity, the ministry said.

Construction on the facility began in 2017 during the administration of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, following a 2015 agreement with Moscow.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Quad is a ‘trusted partnership’ delivering solutions, says PM Modi

Amid the geopolitical tension, what the world needs today is peace, stability and predictability, Prime Minister Narendra Modi underlined at the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit and the Quad Summit in Philippines, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said.

Mr. Misri, in a briefing, said the Prime Minister has just completed a short but very intense visit to Manila, where he participated in the 23rd India-ASEAN Summit, the 21st East Asia Summit and the 7th Quad Leaders Summit.

At each of the three meetings, the Prime Minister underlined that in a world that has seen a great deal of geopolitical tension, flux and stresses and strains, what the world really needs today is peace, stability and predictability, Mr. Misri said.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed for New Delhi after concluding his two-day visit to the Philippines, during which he attended the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit and a meeting of the Quad leaders.
Mr. Modi also met Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., and the two leaders discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in defence, security, trade and investment.
The Prime Minister also discussed regional and global issues of mutual interest with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand on the sidelines of the visit.

Leaders of ‌the four-nation Quad grouping ⁠strongly oppose any destabilising or ‌unilateral actions that seek ‌to ‌change ⁠the status ⁠quo, including by force or coercion, which ‌escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and ‌stability, a joint statement said.
The leaders also ‌expressed grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary ‌export restrictions, the statement added after their ⁠meeting in Manila.

The Quad grouping, following its meeting in Manila, announced the ‘Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration’ which is “ a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness”
“In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer,” the statement added.

articles.title: India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: PM’s adviser
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government

Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that India or any other country could not dictate terms over deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s return home.
Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government.
Talking to reporters at the Bangladesh Secretariat, Mr. Zahed said, “Bangladesh is now an independent, sovereign state standing on firm legal ground and it will reject any unjust terms.”
The premier’s Adviser, however, said he did not believe India would attach conditions to returning Hasina.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Hasina's extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.
He further said: “India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh."
Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal convicted Hasina in November 2025 of crimes against humanity for her role in the crackdown on protesters during the July-August 2024 uprising.
Tried in absentia, she was sentenced to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another. Hasina has rejected the charges and the proceedings.

In a report last week, BBC Bangla said unnamed Indian officials indicated that New Delhi set two main conditions to facilitate Hasina’s return amid Dhaka’s repeated insistence on her extradition under a bilateral treaty despite her repeated stated plan to return home voluntarily to face the legal procedure.
The report said that “under the conditions, India wanted Bangladesh Army to directly receive Hasina either via a military flight to Delhi or at a land border crossing”.
