articles.title: ‘Record horticultural production’ shows increase of 4.36% from 2024-25: Agriculture Ministry
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Significant increase in horticultural production reflects the hard work of India’s farmers and the impact of the Centre’s farmer-friendly policies, Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan says

India’s total horticultural production is expected to reach 3,869.15 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 161.77 lakh tonnes (4.36%) over the production recorded in 2024-25, according to the third advanced estimates of area and production of horticultural crops released by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan in New Delhi on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). In the previous crop season, horticulture production stood at 3,707.38 lakh tonnes.

Mr. Chouhan expressed satisfaction over the projected growth and said the significant increase in horticultural production reflected the hard work of India’s farmers and the impact of the Union government’s farmer-friendly policies. “This record production would not only strengthen the country’s nutritional security but also directly contribute to higher incomes for horticulture farmers,” the Minister said, congratulating farmers across the country for their efforts.

Farmers were increasingly moving beyond traditional crops towards the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers, spices, and plantation crops, including cashew, coconut and cocoa, as well as aromatic and medicinal plants, he said.

“This growing interest in commercial and high-value crops is opening up new avenues of income for farmers while creating fresh opportunities for self-reliance and growth in the agricultural sector,” Mr. Chouhan said, adding that one of the most significant aspects of the latest estimates was increase in production despite a reduction in the area under horticultural cultivation.

“The total area under horticultural crops in 2025-26 is estimated at approximately 297.21 lakh hectares, compared with 301.36 lakh hectares in 2024-25. Despite the decline in cultivated area, production is projected to increase across fruits, vegetables, flowers, plantation crops, and aromatic and medicinal plants,” Mr. Chouhan said.

Fruit production is estimated to rise from 1,176.49 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 1,230.66 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, an increase of 54.18 lakh tonnes or 4.60%. “The improved output is primarily attributed to better production of banana, mango, papaya, apple, pomegranate and jackfruit,” the Union Agriculture Ministry said in a release.

The area under vegetables is estimated to increase from 117.91 lakh hectares to 119.31 lakh hectares. “Vegetable production is projected to rise by 4.35%, from 2,177.97 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 2,272.68 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. The increase is primarily driven by higher production of potato, tomato, brinjal, bottle gourd, cucumber, cabbage, beans and peas,” the release added. Potato and tomato production are both expected to register strong growth. Potato production is estimated at 655.70 lakh tonnes, up 11.95% from 585.71 lakh tonnes in the previous year. Tomato production is projected to increase from 205.99 lakh tonnes to 214.11 lakh tonnes. Onion production is estimated at 288.96 lakh tonnes.

Flower production is projected to rise by approximately 14.45%, from 42.65 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 to 48.82 lakh tonnes in 2025-26. “The area under flower cultivation has also increased to 4.10 lakh hectares,” it added. In the production of plantation crops, including arecanut, coconut, cashew, betel leaves and cocoa. “Their combined production is estimated to increase by 7.56% to 182.64 lakh tonnes. Production of aromatic and medicinal plants is also expected to rise from 9.01 lakh tonnes to 9.28 lakh tonnes,” the Ministry of Agriculture added.

The production of turmeric, garlic, curry leaves and cardamom is also expected to grow. “The total area under spices in 2025-26 is estimated at 47.56 lakh hectares, with production projected at 123.54 lakh tonnes,” the Ministry said.

fullParagraphs: The researchers also identified pharmaceutical compounds such as atomoxetine, domperidone and telmisartan, along with agrochemical-related substances, including diuron and thiamethoxam

Microplastics in the Yamuna in Delhi are accompanied by a complex mixture of organic chemicals, including pharmaceutical residues, pesticides and industrial effluents, with many of these substances classified as human-health and environmental hazards, according to a new study by University of Delhi researchers.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time improves an already perfect classic
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: One of the best Zelda games, Ocarina of Time, has got a gorgeous new remake that is worth playing, if you have a Switch 2

Remakes of past games are pure genius. There are several titles that were mega hits in the 90s or early 2000s when both silicon and game engines were breaking new ground in 3D. Many of those games do not hold up today as well as the pixel game era of the NES and SNES eras do.

Capcom has shown the world that remaking most of their lineup of Resident Evils has been successful. Ubisoft did it too, with Assassin’s Creed: Black Flag Resynced . No one expected Nintendo to jump into the fray, but they did and with style, not only remaking a Zelda game, but one of the cult favorites from the Nintendo 64 era. A game so loved, that it is continuously ranked as one of the greatest games of all times, which is a risky move to remake.
Fortunately, the Ocarina of Time remake not only wears that crown proudly, but is also the only game this year to challenge the sales might of the neon clad tsunami that is Grand Theft Auto VI .

Another saga begins in the cyclic battle of good versus evil, and it revolves around the only boy in the village without a fairy. Entrusted with the fate of the world Link must stop the evil Ganondorf who is intent on grabbing the Tri-force — an artefact that grants the bearer immense power. Guided by the enigmatic fairy Navi, Link must leave the safety of his home, Kokiri Forest, and journey across the sprawling expanse of Hyrule Field, venturing through perilous dungeons, and shift between childhood and adulthood to claim the Master Sword and become the Hero of Time.

Jumping between time from Link’s adult self to his child form is so meta, it will make you feel like you too are jumping through time with him. As an adult, tethered by responsibilities of adulting, you get to jump back to your childhood — something that is more poignant than nostalgia.

In comparison to some of the more sweeping, complex narratives of today’s fantasy games, Ocarina of Time harks back to a simplistic form of storytelling, which was mostly due to cartridge size restrictions. However, it is a template that many of Zelda’s best games have been set on. First-time players are sure to find Link’s story a refreshing one that focuses on core gameplay mechanics and a beautiful reimagining of the world.

The world is gorgeous and while it is not quite open, it does feel like it has got a lot of freedom of movement. It is great to explore all the temples filled with its well-created puzzles that you may remember the solutions for and see the new renditions of iconic places such as Death Mountain, Hyrule Field, Temple of Time and other faithful to their original designs, but are now a lot more fleshed out.
Much of the world has a lot more detail. So rather than rushing through the game, take in your surroundings and scrutinise houses, because there is environmental storytelling peppered everywhere.

Much of the game has been faithfully translated, but thankfully it is free from the oddities of that N64 controller. In addition to updated control mechanics, there are a lot of quality of life improvements, and those who have played Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom , may find the controls familiar. The motions are fluid, and there are some physics-based systems at play, that make everything from the sword clashes feel solid to the sensation of things being physically there in the world as they bounce around.

Combat gains quality of life improvements, inheriting motion aiming from its predecessors making it more snappy, lively and reactive. It lets you acrobatically dodge, backflip and attack enemies, and hits do feel like they actually connect. The enemy AI and animations have been changed to make those fights all the more nail-biting. This being the Switch 2, there are also motion controls to help you use Hookshot, Longshots, bows for some more dynamic ranged combat, if you preferred using this in the newer Zelda games. The addition of jump mechanics do change the dungeons a bit, meaning instead of having the original jump in certain zones, now you actually have to platform across.

articles.title: Assam elephant rescue operation turns violent, eight people arrested
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The incident occurred when Forest personnel tried to guide a female elephant, separated from a herd, back to the jungle it came from

Eight people were detained in central Assam’s Hojai district after they clashed with Forest Department personnel on Monday night (November 16, 2026) during an operation to guide a female elephant back to the jungle it came from.

The Forest officials fired “sera bullets” (pellets) from a pump-action gun to divert the elephant away from a human settlement. Five people were injured in the firing, triggering the mob violence and leaving two personnel injured.
Forest officials claimed three people sustained pellet injuries. The injured, including one of the two personnel, were admitted to a local hospital for treatment.

Divisional Forest Officer Nayan Jyoti Rajbongshi said a herd of elephants from the hills of Karbi Anglong entered the Hawaipur Reserve Forest in Hojai on Monday morning. Barring the female elephant, estimated to be 40 years old, the herd returned to Karbi Anglong a few hours later.
“We received information about the movement of the female elephant, possibly separated from the herd, along a road in a revenue area. We managed to push it into the Hawaipur Reserve Forest,” he said.
However, the elephant emerged from the forest around dusk and headed toward a village. The Forest personnel fired the pellets to drive it away, but some villagers were injured in the process.
“The police brought the situation under control and picked up eight people who clashed with our personnel. The police recorded the statement of our personnel,” Mr. Rajbongshi said.
Wildlife officials said people often obstruct rescue operations by gathering around a wild animal that strays out of a forest.
According to Assam government data tabled in the 126-member Assembly in July, as many as 1,147 people and 246 elephants were killed in human-elephant conflicts in the State since 2016.

articles.title: Chinese scientist fired after child death in gene-editing trial: state media
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The child who died had a rare neurodevelopmental condition called Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome, according to the report
A Chinese scientist who concealed the death of a six-year-old girl in a gene-editing trial has been sacked following a government probe, according to state media.
The girl died last year after receiving experimental gene therapy to correct a non-life-threatening condition -- which was not disclosed in published research, an investigation found in July.

Neuroscientist Zilong Qiu, the trial's lead researcher, had made no mention of the girl in a paper published in the prestigious journal Nature , according to the joint investigation by Science and Retraction Watch .

Qiu was dismissed as deputy director of the Songjiang Research Institute affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, state broadcaster CCTV said Friday, citing a statement from Shanghai authorities.
The reported statement included only Qiu's surname, but referenced the Nature study published on February 18.
Qiu was given a five-year suspension from participating in scientific projects and recorded in a database for "serious breaches of research integrity", the report said.
Another researcher on Qiu's team was sacked and handed a five-year suspension, while several others with ties to the hospital where the trial took place were also punished.
The child who died had a rare neurodevelopmental condition called Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome, according to the report.
The hospital's ethics committee had approved a gene-editing trial to treat the disorder in January 2025, the report said.
The committee terminated the study after the girl died in March due to complications from gene therapy.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Nations must deliver on past promises before committing to lofty climate goals

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Panchkula school attack: Ringing the school bell, raising a safety alarm
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A six-year-old girl was allegedly assaulted by an eight-year-old classmate in a classroom in Panchkula, with CCTV footage capturing the attack. The incident raises concerns about school safety, supervision, and the influence of violent video games on children

The school’s auto-rickshaw arrived at its usual time around noon on October 28. Homemaker Aarti (name changed to protect privacy) took a quick, reassuring look at her six-year-old daughter’s uniform and schoolbag before waving her off with a smile. However, at 3:30 p.m., when the auto-rickshaw driver went to pick her up from her school in Haryana ’s Panchkula district, the girl was nowhere to be found. Her bag was kept at the school’s reception area.

The driver informed her family, who live just five minutes away from the school, and her father came rushing. As he called out her name, his voice grew louder with every frantic step towards the school building. He asked the teachers about his daughter’s whereabouts, and they joined him in his search. Soon, a boy approached him, asked his daughter’s name and confirmed whether he was looking for her. When the father nodded, the boy led him to a classroom on the first floor, telling him that someone had beaten her up.

articles.title: Prince William, Princess Kate to meet PM Modi in New Delhi this week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The couple will arrive in Mumbai today for the annual Earthshot Prize ceremony; the visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry

The Prince and Princess of Wales, William and Catherine (Kate), are due to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Wednesday. The couple will arrive in Mumbai for a three-day visit, with public engagements kicking off mid-morning on Monday (November 16, 2026). The visit is focused around the Prince’s annual Earthshot Prize, which will be given out on Tuesday evening at a ceremony in the city.

The couple, who were originally scheduled to spend their entire visit in Mumbai, will now conclude it with a meeting with Mr. Modi. Their schedule was changed on Sunday after Mr. Modi’s travel plans were confirmed, the Sunday Times reported. The Prime Minister is due to return from the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) Summit in the Philippines on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry. Prince William played a round of cricket with cricketers Sourav Ganguly, Brian Lara and England captain Joe Root outside Buckingham Palace last month to promote his environmental prize.

Prince William, 44, is the heir to the British throne and shares a passion for the environment like his father, King Charles III. The Earthshot Prize was instituted by the Prince in 2020 and offers each of five finalists £1 million (approximately ₹12.5 crore) for solutions to pressing environmental problems.
India has produced more finalists for the prize than any other country, Kensington Palace said.

Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek (the American actor who played one-time Mumbai resident Freddie Mercury in the 2018 film, Bohemian Rhapsody ), are among those expected to attend the awards ceremony, hosted by celebrity talk show host Karan Johar. British pop group Take That will perform at Tuesday’s event.
When in Mumbai, the Prince and Princess will also attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony — the culmination of a contest among 15,000 schools across 24 States.

“The future of the U.K.-India partnership will not be shaped by our governments alone, it will be shaped by our people and this visit is a wonderful opportunity to celebrate those deep personal connections between our countries,” said Ben Mellor, Acting British High Commissioner to India, according to PTI.

This is Prince William and Princess Kate’s second official visit to India and the Princess’s first major overseas trip since she was treated for cancer in 2024 and had to step back from official duties.

articles.title: Boy electrocuted by snapped stay wire in Malappuram; Minister orders probe
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 13-year-old boy died of electrocution after coming into contact with a snapped stay wire attached to an electric pole in a paddy field in Malappuram on Sunday (November 15).
The deceased, identified as Junaid, son of Shihabudheen of Cherumukku in Tirurangadi, had gone to the field with friends to watch a tractor plough the land, the police said.

Residents said Junaid’s friends tried to rescue him, but the tractor driver stopped them from approaching the wire, saving them from a similar fate. They alleged that officials of the Keralam State Electricity Board (KSEB) took time to disconnect the power supply despite repeated calls for help.
The incident triggered protests by residents who accused KSEB officials of serious negligence.
Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph ordered an immediate inquiry into the incident and directed officials to ensure compensation for the bereaved family.

In a statement, Mr. Joseph said that he had directed the Deputy Chief Engineer of KSEB, Tirurangadi, to submit a factual report immediately. “Strict disciplinary action will be taken against those found responsible for any lapse,” he added.
The Minister said safety inspections would be intensified across the State to prevent the recurrence of such incidents.
Meanwhile, the KSEB, in a statement, apologised for the incident and said that an impartial and detailed inquiry into the circumstances leading to the accident would be conducted.
The KSEB urged consumers to report electricity-related safety hazards by sending photographs and details through WhatsApp to 94960-10101.

articles.title: My entire life has been a struggle, says Bilkis Bano at GIO conference in Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage.

“My entire life has been a struggle,” Bilkis Bano, the Gujarat riots survivor who has emerged as an icon of resilience with her prolonged legal battle for justice, said in Kochi on Sunday (November 15).
Ms. Bano made the compelling remark as she inaugurated the International Conference on Women organised by the State committee of the Girls Islamic Organisation (GIO) in the city.

“Everyone knows my life story, don’t they? There is no need to say anything more about it,” she said in a brief address. Ms. Bano was gang-raped and lost seven members of her family, including her three-year-old daughter, in the 2002 riots.
Thanking those who invited her, she said, “May we continue to live with such love and peace every day, staying together all our lives.”

Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage. “The family had to relocate several times, and her rights were denied. They had to repeatedly bring instances of injustice to the attention of those in positions of power. What happened to Bilkis is now known to the entire world. May her struggle inspire every woman to find the strength to raise her voice for her rights,” he said.
The conference was presided over by GIO State president K. Shifana. Jamia Millia Islamia student leader Nousheen Farooq was the chief guest.

Saria Cheruvallil, Professor at Coventry University, UK; Dalia Saleh, researcher at the University of Cambridge; Reem Mahmoud Al Haddad, Palestinian writer and journalist; Jamaat-e-Islami national secretary A. Rahmathunnisa; and Jamaat-e-Islami Keralam ameer P. Mujeeb Rahman were among those who spoke at various sessions.

Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage.

“My entire life has been a struggle,” Bilkis Bano, the Gujarat riots survivor who has emerged as an icon of resilience with her prolonged legal battle for justice, said in Kochi on Sunday (November 15).

Ms. Bano made the compelling remark as she inaugurated the International Conference on Women organised by the State committee of the Girls Islamic Organisation (GIO) in the city.

“Everyone knows my life story, don’t they? There is no need to say anything more about it,” she said in a brief address. Ms. Bano was gang-raped and lost seven members of her family, including her three-year-old daughter, in the 2002 riots.

Thanking those who invited her, she said, “May we continue to live with such love and peace every day, staying together all our lives.”

Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage. “The family had to relocate several times, and her rights were denied. They had to repeatedly bring instances of injustice to the attention of those in positions of power. What happened to Bilkis is now known to the entire world. May her struggle inspire every woman to find the strength to raise her voice for her rights,” he said.

The conference was presided over by GIO State president K. Shifana. Jamia Millia Islamia student leader Nousheen Farooq was the chief guest.

Saria Cheruvallil, Professor at Coventry University, UK; Dalia Saleh, researcher at the University of Cambridge; Reem Mahmoud Al Haddad, Palestinian writer and journalist; Jamaat-e-Islami national secretary A. Rahmathunnisa; and Jamaat-e-Islami Keralam ameer P. Mujeeb Rahman were among those who spoke at various sessions.

articles.title: Guest teachers in Haryana hold mock Assembly, demand regularisation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Guest teachers in Haryana schools held a mock Assembly at the Mini Secretariat in Kurukshetra on Saturday, demanding regularisation under the three-year policy notified in 2014 in accordance with court orders.

Organised on the call of the Rajkiya Anubandhit Adhyapak Sangh, the symbolic Assembly passed a resolution seeking regularisation of guest teachers by an overwhelming majority. The resolution will be submitted to Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini at his camp office in Kurukshetra on November 29. The teachers will also hold a rally in Delhi on December 12 and submit the resolution to the President.

Teachers said guest teachers had been serving in government schools for the past 21 years and contributing to the State’s education system, but the government continued to keep them in temporary employment arrangements instead of regularising their services. Following the court orders, the Haryana School Education Department issued speaking orders denying regular status to the guest teachers.
They said the mock Assembly was organised to raise questions concerning the regularisation of guest teachers, judicial decisions and the government’s accountability on a public platform.

The event was attended by educationists, intellectuals, employee union leaders from various departments, School Management Committee representatives, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha, student and youth organisations, advocates’ unions, writers’ associations, university professors, the Jan Sangharsh Manch, Kurukshetra, and social activists.
These teachers, appointed between 2005 and 2008, are working as junior basic teachers, trained graduate teachers, and post graduate teachers.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The growth in India’s merchandise exports in October, the fastest in five years and faster than import growth, indicates that volumes of exports are growing along with prices
India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house

Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: As diabetes spikes in Kashmir, the health lens turns to the fabled wazwan
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Subsistence agriculture and labour-intensive living has been replaced by urbanisation and declining physical activity, while traditional dietary patterns persist largely unchanged, the doctor-authors of Diabetes Simplified for Kashmir say

The Kashmiri wazwan , an array of dishes adding up to 4,500-5,500 calories partaken during festivals and weddings, is one of the key cultural factors contributing to a spike in cases of diabetes in Kashmir, experts said.

Kashmir’s social life is organised around large, meat-centred feasts, most visibly the wazwan served at weddings or on Eid. Diabetes Simplified for Kashmir , a book released on World Diabetes Day (November 14), said the multi-course meal can run to over 30 mutton and chicken preparations, with the calorie intake “several times the average daily requirement”.

“Such exposure accumulates rather than occurs in isolation, and repeated post-prandial glucose and lipid excursions of this magnitude plausibly contribute to the region’s rising dysglycaemia burden,” the book, co-authored by endocrinologists Mohammad Hayat Bhat and Shahnawaz Mir, and cardiologist Nasir Shams, stated.
Degchis (traditional heavy-bottomed cooking pots) filled with wazwan dishes at a wedding feast in Srinagar. | Photo Credit: Reuters

J&K has witnessed a spike in the incidence of diabetes in the past three years. The Union Territory screened more than 2.15 million people for diabetes; 48,623 individuals have been diagnosed to have diabetes, according to data from the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. In 2025-2026, 2.84 million people were screened and 85,948 were found to have diabetes. “In the past three years, J&K added 2.18 lakh new patients to its diabetes burden,” the Ministry’s data suggested.
Apart from more universally seen factors, including poor physical activity and consumption of tobacco, the book identifies Kashmir’s unique lifestyle among the contributing factors.

“Kashmir’s daily plate remains rice-centric with rice typically supplying the bulk of meal volume and carbohydrate load. Large portions of rice translate directly into high postprandial glycaemic load,” it said.

“Type 2 diabetes prevalence in Kashmir has risen sharply within a single generation. A survey in 1999 found known diabetes in just 1.89% of adults, with 4.25% undiagnosed. Recent Indian Council of Medical Research-INDIA data show 7.8% prevalence,” the authors said, attributing the rising incidence of Type 2 diabetes to lifestyle in Kashmir.

The book noted that such a rapid shift cannot reflect genetic change. “It points instead to a compressed nutrition and lifestyle transition, as subsistence agriculture and labour-intensive living have been replaced by urbanisation and declining physical activity, while traditional dietary patterns — rice-centric meals, salt tea, preserved winter foods, and elaborate festive feasting — persist largely unchanged,” the experts said.

They also attributed the rise in cases of diabetes to Kashmir’s winters. “The glycaemic and fat load of the traditional meat and generous portion sizes do not act in isolation. Their convergence with a pronounced winter sedentary period appears to produce a compounding rather than merely additive metabolic burden across the Kashmiri annual cycle, in which periods of highest intake coincide with the lowest levels of expenditure,” they added.

articles.title: Police bust examination cheating racket in Jammu; 14 arrested
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Electronic devices, including wireless radio sets allegedly intended to facilitate the transmission of answers to candidates inside the examination halls, were found and seized by police

In a major intelligence-led operation, police on Sunday (November 15, 2026) arrested 14 suspected individuals for allegedly attempting to facilitate cheating in the Jammu and Kashmir Services Selection Board (SSB) Finance Assistant Examination in Jammu, an official said.

Acting on credible intelligence inputs regarding a group of individuals allegedly conspiring to facilitate the use of unfair means during the examination, the Jammu Police took swift action and apprehended the suspected facilitators along with electronic equipment allegedly intended for the commission of the offence, a spokesperson of the force said.

He said preliminary inputs suggested that the suspects had devised a mechanism to transmit answers to selected candidates appearing in the examination through modern electronic communication technology.

Taking prompt cognisance of the intelligence inputs, multiple police teams were formed and strategically deployed around identified examination centres to detect and apprehend the suspected facilitators and prevent any attempt to compromise the fairness and integrity of the examination process, the official said.
The 14 suspects were apprehended from peripheral and adjoining locations of various examination centres before the commencement of the test.

Electronic devices, including wireless radio sets allegedly intended to facilitate the transmission of answers to candidates inside the examination halls, were found and seized by police, the spokesperson said.
Three FIRs have been registered at the Domana police station under relevant penal provisions, he added.
A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has also been constituted to conduct a comprehensive and thorough probe into the matter, he said.

He said the probe will focus on uncovering the entire network involved in the alleged conspiracy, establishing the specific roles of the suspects and beneficiaries, tracing the source and procurement of the electronic communication devices, and ascertaining the possible involvement of other individuals.

Police reiterate their commitment to ensuring a fair, transparent and peaceful conduct of competitive examinations and warn against any attempt to undermine the integrity of the examination system, the spokesperson said, adding that strict legal action shall be taken against those found involved in such unlawful activities.

articles.title: Jawaharlal Nehru through an intelligence prism

fullParagraphs: Critics of Jawaharlal Nehru have spared no effort to portray him as being rosy-eyed and naive about China; yet, memoirs of Bhola Nath Mullik, the intelligence chief who served under Nehru for almost the entire duration his Prime Ministership make it clear this was far from the truth

It is difficult to say or write anything about India’s first Prime Minister that has not already been said or written. What he comes across as when looked at through the prism of his intelligence chief is, however, a dimension of his working life that has not been adequately commented upon.

articles.title: India’s relation with ASEAN at heart of Act East Policy, says PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is visiting Manila on November 16-17 to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit at the invitation of Philippine President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (November 16, 2026) embarked on a visit to Manila in the Philippines to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on November 17, 2026. Mr. Modi is attending the summits at the invitation of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.

Ahead of his departure, Mr. Modi, in a statement, said, “Our relationship with ASEAN countries is at the heart of India’s Act East Policy and occupies a central place in our MAHASAGAR vision. Our ties, rooted in centuries of civilizational exchanges, have grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people relations.”

“At the ASEAN-India Summit, I look forward to working with fellow leaders to build on the progress of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and give further momentum to our shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity,” he added.
Talking about The East Asia Summit, Mr. Modi said that it ‘provides an important platform for dialogue on regional and global challenges’.
“I look forward to exchanging views with participating leaders on strengthening peace, stability and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific,” the Prime Minister said.
Mr. Modi also said he looks forward to interacting with the vibrant Indian community in the Philippines ‘whose contributions strengthen the bonds of friendship between our two countries’.
“I am confident that the visit will impart new energy to India’s partnership with ASEAN and reinforce our collective commitment to a peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific,” he added.
A meeting of the leaders of the Quad group — comprising the U.S., India, Australia and Japan — is scheduled to be held in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit, a senior U.S. official said.

The meeting of the Quad leaders, the first in two years, will bring together Prime Minister Narendra Modi, U.S. President Donald Trump, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
The last meeting of Quad leaders was chaired by then U.S. President Joe Biden in Delaware on September 21, 2024.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi is visiting Manila on November 16-17 to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit at the invitation of Philippine President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (November 16, 2026) embarked on a visit to Manila in the Philippines to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on November 17, 2026. Mr. Modi is attending the summits at the invitation of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.

Ahead of his departure, Mr. Modi, in a statement, said, “Our relationship with ASEAN countries is at the heart of India’s Act East Policy and occupies a central place in our MAHASAGAR vision. Our ties, rooted in centuries of civilizational exchanges, have grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people relations.”

“At the ASEAN-India Summit, I look forward to working with fellow leaders to build on the progress of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and give further momentum to our shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity,” he added.

Talking about The East Asia Summit, Mr. Modi said that it ‘provides an important platform for dialogue on regional and global challenges’.

“I look forward to exchanging views with participating leaders on strengthening peace, stability and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific,” the Prime Minister said.

Mr. Modi also said he looks forward to interacting with the vibrant Indian community in the Philippines ‘whose contributions strengthen the bonds of friendship between our two countries’.

“I am confident that the visit will impart new energy to India’s partnership with ASEAN and reinforce our collective commitment to a peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific,” he added.

A meeting of the leaders of the Quad group — comprising the U.S., India, Australia and Japan — is scheduled to be held in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit, a senior U.S. official said.

The meeting of the Quad leaders, the first in two years, will bring together Prime Minister Narendra Modi, U.S. President Donald Trump, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

articles.title: Carney says Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if Trump trade talks fail
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Mr. Carney said any Chinese investment would have to involve substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than simply assembling imported parts

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that Canada could turn to Chinese automakers if trade negotiations with U.S. President Donald Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry.

“We have the best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, full opportunity, in an integrated North American market,” Mr. Carney told reporters in Cambodia. “That market has become less integrated because of U.S. trade actions.”

Mr. Carney said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) in Manila, Philippines, that any trade agreement with Washington must leave Canada with a viable auto industry. He said on Monday (November 16) that negotiations with the United States remain his priority, but their outcome could determine whether Canada pursues alternatives involving European, Chinese or Japanese automakers.
Asked whether potential Chinese investment was leverage in the U.S. negotiations, Mr. Carney replied: “It's not leverage. But action, reaction.”

“If they're not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities,” Mr. Carney said of Canada's auto workers and manufacturing assets. “Canada is going to move forward either way.”

The Detroit Three — Ford, General Motors and Stellantis — operate factories across Canada, the United States and Mexico, with parts sometimes crossing borders multiple times before a vehicle is completed. Mr. Trump has repeatedly pushed automakers to move production to the United States from Canada.

Mr. Carney said any Chinese investment would have to involve substantial manufacturing in Canada rather than simply assembling imported parts. He said it would require proper labour standards, manufacturing facilities and domestic supply chains that expand over time, including Canadian critical minerals used in electric vehicles.
“It's not just about kit cars,” he said. “There has to be a manufacturing aspect involved.”

Under the January agreement, Canada reduced its 100% tariff on Chinese electric vehicles to 6.1%, initially allowing up to 49,000 vehicles annually, with the cap increasing over time. In exchange, China agreed to lower tariffs on Canadian agricultural products, including canola.
Mr. Carney said at the time that he expected the agreement to attract Chinese investment in Canada's auto industry and create jobs.

articles.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

Supporters of deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina ’s Awami League party staged violent demonstrations in her hometown of Gopalganj on Sunday (November 15, 2026), attacking police vehicles and installations amid growing political tensions over her stated plan to return to the country in December.
Editorial | In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government.

Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over her government’s crackdown on protesters. She has rejected the charges and the proceedings.
Ms. Hasina, 79, has repeatedly said since July that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and face legal proceedings, despite the death sentence against her.

The Bangladesh government has been seeking her extradition from India under a bilateral treaty. It has also declined a request made by a London-based law firm on Ms. Hasina’s behalf for a passport to facilitate her return.
Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that Bangladesh had completed the legal process to secure Ms. Hasina’s return and that the decision now rested with India.

Bangladesh has also linked progress on Ms. Hasina’s extradition to a possible visit to India by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman , saying her return and that of other fugitives sought by Dhaka would help create a conducive environment for the visit.
India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in New Delhi that Ms. Hasina’s extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.

articles.title: Yemeni government forces retreat from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February

Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday (November 15, 2026) that they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their ​main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The announcement signalled the apparent ‌end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the ​Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that ⁠squeezed oil exports.

Sunday's announcement of a government retreat raises the prospect of new Houthi advances towards Aden, and underscores the predicament faced by Saudi Arabia in trying to stop the Houthis' drone and missile attacks on the kingdom. The government ‌forces have been based in Aden on the southern coast since 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February.

"The Southern Armed Forces announce the ⁠implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate," the main military force fighting for Yemen's government in the south of the country said in a statement.
"This step is taken based ​on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, ‌and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats."
There was no immediate response from the Houthis, or from Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government's main international ally.

Yemen's decade-long civil war, which had been dormant since 2022, abruptly reignited this summer as a ‌spillover from the Iran conflict. The Houthis made rapid gains to capture the coast along the ​Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which controls access to it, while besieging government forces in Taiz, the country's third-biggest city, in mountains above the approach to Aden.

A ⁠Saudi-backed government offensive last month rapidly retook key positions around the strait, notably Dhubab, but failed to drive the Houthis entirely away from the area or to retake the city of al-Mocha further up the coast.

The ‌Houthis have responded by intensifying drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, grounding flights with strikes on its main airports as well as setting global energy markets on edge by targeting energy facilities.

articles.title: Keralam’s orchids endure from highway trees to salt-sprayed shores
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: A rescue-and-relocation project has saved over 27,000 native orchids from roadside trees felled in Keralam, and more than 71% were still alive, ​5,224 had flowered, and 1,934 had produced capsules after one to two years, offering a low-cost model for conservation
With their dazzling colours and ambrosial aromas, orchids are one of earth’s most distinctive flowering plant families.
They are found on every continent except Antarctica and count over 29,500 native species worldwide.
According to Orchids of India: A Pictorial Guide (2019), published by the Botanical Survey of India, Keralam accounts for more than a third of the 307 endemic orchids reported from India.
The State’s native orchid density is comparable to South American countries like Costa Rica, Viswambharan Sarasan, a research leader at the Royal Botanic Gardens in the U.K., said.
But habitat loss and fragmentation are increasingly threatening the State’s orchid diversity.
“As a child, I saw these orchids on coconut palms in our backyard [in Keralam],” he said. “But now they are disappearing from everywhere.”
However, according to Dr. Sarasan, relocating orchids from development sites or disturbed areas can reduce these losses.

Over the last three years, under Dr. Sarasan’s leadership, a research team at the KSCSTE-Malabar Botanical Garden and Institute for Plant Sciences in Calicut has rescued more than 27,000 native orchids growing on trees from being destroyed in road-widening activities in the State.

“I went to Kerala six, seven years ago, pitching this idea of growing orchids in large hubs where people congregate, such as the Napier Museum or the Kanakakunnu Palace in Thiruvananthapuram,” Dr. Sarasan, who hails from the capital city of Keralam, said.

With funding from the Royal Society International Exchanges programme, the project aimed to collect orchids from Keralam’s forests and rural areas. “However, we quickly realised there isn’t much diversity in the south,” he said.

Water adventure activities at the Harangi backwaters have been temporarily suspended following the death of a tourist couple in a speedboat accident recently.

Kodagu Deputy Commissioner S.J. Somashekar on Monday (November 16) visited the Harangi backwaters in Kushalnagar taluk, where the couple, from Gujarat, died after their speedboat capsized during a water adventure activity. The couple’s two children were rescued.
Mr. Somashekar inspected the accident site and gathered details about the incident and the safety measures in place.
The accident, however, has raised serious concerns over safety arrangements at the popular tourist destination, which attracts a large number of visitors.
Mr. Somashekar said adequate precautionary measures should have been in place to prevent such accidents during water sports activities.

According to local residents, a private company has been operating water adventure activities at the Harangi backwaters since 2023. The couple were travelling in a speedboat when it reportedly lost control and capsized while negotiating a turn. Both were trapped underneath the boat and died.
Later, Mr. Somashekar obtained details about the hi-tech toilet facility constructed near the Dubare river rafting site.
He also visited and inspected the Basavanahalli residential school in the taluk.
Cauvery Neeravari Nigam superintending engineer Satish, assistant executive engineer Puttaswamy, tahsildar Ramesh and Public Works Department executive engineer Prabhu were among those present.

The couple’s two children were rescued; Kodagu Deputy Commissioner inspected the accident site and gathered details about the incident and the safety measures in place.

Water adventure activities at the Harangi backwaters have been temporarily suspended following the death of a tourist couple in a speedboat accident recently.

Kodagu Deputy Commissioner S.J. Somashekar on Monday (November 16) visited the Harangi backwaters in Kushalnagar taluk, where the couple, from Gujarat, died after their speedboat capsized during a water adventure activity. The couple’s two children were rescued.

Mr. Somashekar inspected the accident site and gathered details about the incident and the safety measures in place.

The accident, however, has raised serious concerns over safety arrangements at the popular tourist destination, which attracts a large number of visitors.

Mr. Somashekar said adequate precautionary measures should have been in place to prevent such accidents during water sports activities.

According to local residents, a private company has been operating water adventure activities at the Harangi backwaters since 2023. The couple were travelling in a speedboat when it reportedly lost control and capsized while negotiating a turn. Both were trapped underneath the boat and died.

Later, Mr. Somashekar obtained details about the hi-tech toilet facility constructed near the Dubare river rafting site.

He also visited and inspected the Basavanahalli residential school in the taluk.

Cauvery Neeravari Nigam superintending engineer Satish, assistant executive engineer Puttaswamy, tahsildar Ramesh and Public Works Department executive engineer Prabhu were among those present.

articles.title: Samples of 23 persons tested H5N1 negative, says Health Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: At least 16 poultry farms in Cuddalore district affected by Avian Influenza; continuous surveillance being done by the Public Health Department, says Arunraj

Minister for Health K.G. Arunraj on Monday said that samples of 23 persons, who are mostly poultry workers and veterinary staff in affected areas, have tested negative for Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (H5N1).

Addressing reporters on the sidelines of inspection of government hospitals in Vellore town, Dr. Arunraj said that 54 persons, who are mostly poultry workers and veterinary staff, were identified as these people were associated with affected poultry farms in Cuddalore. Of them, samples of 27 persons were collected and sent for testing. Results of 23 samples that have come so far have tested negative of H5N1 avian influenza virus. “The findings of 23 samples that were tested shows that the virus has not spread among humans. Despite sample results, surveillance has been intensified in affected areas,” he said.

The Minister further said that at least 16 poultry farms in Cuddalore district were affected with Avian Influenza (H5N1). The Department of Public Health has conducted 27 medical camps in a 10 kms radius of the affected farms as part of preventive measures. Continuous surveillance is also being done by the Public Health Department in coordination with the Department of Animal Husbandry, he said.

The Minister asserted that adequate stock of medicines especially anti-rabies and snake bites were available in government hospitals. The State government has also taken steps to fill around 2,500 vacant posts including pharmacists, doctors, nurses in government hospitals. The government has recently filled 4727 nurses in a transparent manner in the State. An order to fill vacant posts will be issued soon, he said.

Asked about setting up of new medical colleges in newly formed districts such as Ranipet, Tirupattur and Kallakuruchi, Mr. Arunraj said that the issue will be taken up to Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. Thereafter, necessary steps will be taken to set up new medical colleges in these new districts.

The Minister inspected Government Medical College Hospital and Pentland Government Multi speciality Hospital in Vellore town where he interacted with patients, hospital staff and health officials in the presence of Collector P.S. Leela Alex. Later, Mr. Arunraj attended the graduation ceremony at CMC in Vellore.

articles.title: GRAAM’s relocated head office inaugurated in Mysuru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The relocated head office is expected to serve as a platform for dialogue, collaboration and knowledge exchange among researchers, policymakers, academic institutions, development partners and community representatives
The relocated head office of Grassroots Research and Advocacy Movement (GRAAM) was inaugurated on its new premises on Vishwamanava Double Road in Kuvempunagar in Mysuru on Monday (November 16).

The relocated head office is expected to serve as a platform for dialogue, collaboration and knowledge exchange among researchers, policymakers, academic institutions, development partners and community representatives, according to a statement here by GRAAM, which is a not-for-profit public policy research and development think tank based out of Mysuru.

The inauguration, which was was done by T.S. Srivatsa, Krishnaraja MLA, was also marked by the unveiling of the GRAAM Journey Wall, titled ‘Sankalpadinda Sadhaneyedege’ (’From Resolve to Achievement’), showcasing the organisation’s 15-year journey, achievements and key milestones.

Mr. Srivatsa highlighted several priorities for Mysuru’s overall development. articles.title: Maximise STP utilisation for ‘green water’ supply, says HMWSSB MD Ashok Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a push to conserve groundwater and expand the use of treated wastewater, Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director Ashok Reddy has directed officials to maximise the utilisation of Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) and strengthen the supply of ‘green water’ across the city.

During inspections of the Nagole and Patel Cheruvu STPs on Monday, he reviewed treatment operations, tanker filling facilities and the distribution of treated water, and instructed officials to ensure that STPs operate at their full capacity and to prepare detailed reports on engineering requirements, power consumption and operational costs.

At Patel Cheruvu, he joined local legislator Bandari Lakshma Reddy, and flagged off green water tankers and appealed to construction companies to use treated water instead of drinking water or groundwater for construction activities.

He also visited an apartment construction site, where he explored the feasibility of supplying treated water through dedicated pipelines. Officials were asked to identify large construction projects requiring water for at least two years and examine the possibility of laying 300–400 metre pipeline connections for continuous supply.

articles.title: Modi government favouring corporates at the cost of farmers: Vijoo Krishnan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) national general secretary Vijoo Krishnan urged farmers and agricultural workers to intensify their united struggles against what he described as the anti-farmer and anti-people policies of the Union government.

Addressing the 36th national conference of the AIKS at G.M. Goud Convention Hall in Nalgonda, Mr. Krishnan alleged that the Union government’s economic policies were aligned with American interests. He expressed concern over free trade agreements with the United States, New Zealand and the European Union, warning that they could adversely affect Indian agriculture and threaten farmers’ livelihoods.
Mr. Krishnan alleged that the Union government was facilitating the transfer of mineral resources, forests and agricultural land to major corporate groups at nominal prices.
He said significant land reforms and redistribution of land to the poor had taken place in States where communist movements were strong or communist-led governments had been in power.

Highlighting the plight of tenant farmers, he said they continued to face difficulties in accessing institutional credit, subsidies and compensation for crop losses. Telangana had more than 20 lakh tenant farmers and Andhra Pradesh over 30 lakh, but the respective State governments had failed to provide adequate assistance to them, he claimed.
He further said drought conditions prevailed in more than 342 districts across the country and demanded immediate relief measures from the Union and State governments.

Mr. Krishnan also criticised the VB-G RAM G scheme, alleging that it could adversely affect the rural poor. He opposed the acquisition of agricultural and forest lands for eco-tourism and other development projects and demanded justice for displaced communities.

Recalling the farmers’ agitation on the borders of Delhi, he accused the Union government of failing to honour the written assurances given when the protest was withdrawn. He demanded implementation of the recommendations of the M.S. Swaminathan Commission to ensure remunerative prices for agricultural produce.

articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: According to economists, not only will this high wholesale inflation soon translate into higher consumer prices, but it also means an interest rate hike is nearly certain, which would dampen economic sentiment

Wholesale inflation in India surged to 12.3% in October 2026, the second consecutive month of double-digit inflation, official data released on Monday (November 16, 2026) showed. Fuel prices continue to be the main reason for the price rise, with the crude petroleum and natural gas sectors seeing inflation of more than 70%.

The new series of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry has data that goes back to only April 2024 and so a historical analysis for a longer duration is not possible. However, the data shows that inflation in October was the highest since at least then.
This data follows the release of Consumer Price Index data last week that showed that even retail inflation had climbed above the Reserve Bank of India’s upper comfort mark of 6% in October 2026.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, it is only a matter of time before wholesale inflation translates into a further increase in the prices consumers pay.

“It has been seen that manufactured goods in particular have witnessed an increase of 9.5%, with high inflation rates in textiles, tobacco products, chemicals, rubber products, metals and electrical equipment,” Mr. Sabnavis pointed out. “This will pressurise companies into increasing their product prices at some point of time.”
“This passthrough will get reflected in the core part of the CPI in the coming months depending on the actions of industry,” he added.

Further, as Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive argues, the high WPI inflation makes a rate hike by the RBI in December a near certainty, which would have a further dampening effect on the economy.

“The sharp rise in WPI inflation to 12.39% in October 2026 reinforces the inflationary concerns already reflected in elevated retail inflation readings,” Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive said. “As a result, a rate hike by the RBI in the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting [in December] now looks almost certain.”

“Higher interest rates may impact lending activity, investments, and consumption, while sentiment across the financial sector could remain under pressure,” Ms. Pandya added. “With geopolitical tensions resurfacing in the Russia-Ukraine region, risks to inflation and economic growth have become even more pronounced.”

Within the WPI, food inflation climbed to 8.3% in October 2026, the highest in 22 months. The overall fuel and power category saw inflation jump to nearly 33% in the same month, compared to about 26% in September 2026. These high levels were, however, also a result of a low base, since this segment of the WPI was in contraction for large parts of 2025.

articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.
The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.
