articles.title: SpaceX’s Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center within the next few months
SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday (November 14, 2026), caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.

It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch.
Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad.
“Can you believe it?” shouted SpaceX commentator Dan Huot.

SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, intended for moon and Mars travel. Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique.

NASA welcomed Saturday’s news. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Musk’s ambitions are even grander: He wants to launch a fleet of Starships to build a city on Mars.

The world’s largest and most powerful rocket — a 407-foot (124-metre) behemoth — blasted off late Friday afternoon from SpaceX’s Starship base near the U.S.-Mexican border. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites.

Starship continued circling the world 165 miles (265 kilometres) up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. The spacecraft completed 14 laps around Earth, outshining the previous mission’s one to two laps.
It was SpaceX’s 15th flight of a full-scale Starship since 2023 and its only second trip to orbit.
SpaceX reported that everything on the spacecraft, including its vital heat shield, appeared to work well.

articles.title: Jensen Huang | AI rainmaker meets his Waterloo

fullParagraphs: The Nvidia chief’s abrupt exit marks a stunning fall from grace for the man who built the hardware foundation of the AI revolution, forged deep ties with Silicon Valley’s tech leaders and expanded the company’s reach across every layer of the AI stack

“In another life, Jensen Huang might have been a teacher,” says Tae Kim in his book The Nvidia Way . Whether he likes it or not, the Nvidia co-founder’s reality has now been reset, forcing him back to his idiosyncratic style of solving problems: diagramming on a whiteboard. But this time he won’t get a clean start as the scandal-hit former chief of Nvidia will face intense scrutiny over his affair with a Chinese businesswoman who is at the centre of an alleged spy scandal.

Within days of reports emerging about Mr. Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, The New York Times reported a second relationship, with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s head of healthcare and one of his direct reports. By then, the controversy had come to a head, forcing Mr. Huang to resign as CEO of Nvidia, the company he had built from scratch.
Global & Diplomatic Brief: Jensen Huang | AI rainmaker meets his Waterloo. This development underscores India's strategic autonomy and pragmatic engagement in bilateral and multilateral diplomacy.

articles.title: Statewide vaccination drive to protect children aged 10 and 16 against tetanus and diphtheria
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Children receive Pentavalent vaccines when very young as part of the immunisation programme, and the TD vaccine is administered to provide additional protection
A vaccination drive will be held across the State from December 3 to 5 to protect children against diphtheria and tetanus, which are potentially life-threatening yet preventable bacterial diseases.

According to a release from the Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare, the TD (Tetanus-Diphtheria) vaccine will be administered to children who have completed 10 and 16 years of age. The health department aims to cover more than 95% of children in this age bracket during the drive, which will be conducted across government and private schools and intermediate colleges on three days.

Children receive Pentavalent vaccines when very young as part of the immunisation programme, and the TD vaccine is administered to provide additional protection. According to the release, protection during adolescence is also essential, as diphtheria and tetanus are infectious diseases that can cause serious illness and even prove fatal.
Children who have completed 10 years of age should be administered the TD-10 vaccine, while those who have completed 16 years should receive the TD-16 vaccine.

Before the drive begins, ANMs have been directed to prepare a list of government and private schools and intermediate colleges in their jurisdictions and collect details of children eligible for vaccination. They should also identify those who did not attend schools or colleges. They have also been tasked with arranging the required vaccine doses, medical supplies, among other things.

Health and Family Welfare Commissioner and National Health Mission Director K.V.N. Chakradhar Babu directed District Medical and Health Officers, District Immunisation Officers and medical officers working in Primary Health Centres to conduct coordination meetings with the departments of Women and Child Welfare, Education, Minority Welfare, Panchayat Raj and Municipal Administration and Urban Development for the effective implementation of the drive.

Mr. Chakradhar Babu directed district health officials to continuously monitor the drive and inspect vaccination centres to ensure adequate vaccine availability, anaphylaxis kits, and other medical supplies to treat any emergencies.
Once vaccination is completed, digital certificates of the same should be issued to all beneficiaries and the same information should be uploaded on online health portals, the official said.

articles.title: Dhinakaran, Vasan urge Vijay to protect interests of T.N. farmers in Mekedatu issue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a statement, Mr. Dhinakaran accused Mr. Vijay of failing to discharge his responsibility to protect farmers’ livelihoods for the sake of retaining power, alleging this had emboldened D.K. Shivakumar to persist with the Mekedatu project

AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Sunday (November 15, 2026) accused Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay of shedding crocodile tears over the Mekedatu dam issue and said the latter had to choose between his party’s alliance with the Congress and the livelihoods of Tamil Nadu farmers.

In a statement, Mr. Dhinakaran accused Mr. Vijay of failing to discharge his responsibility to protect farmers’ livelihoods for the sake of retaining power, alleging this had emboldened Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to persist with the Mekedatu project.

Condemning Mr. Shivakumar’s remarks on constructing the dam across the Cauvery, Mr. Dhinakaran urged Mr. Vijay to exert political pressure through the Congress leadership to stop the project, warning failure to do so would amount to a betrayal of Tamil Nadu farmers.

Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) leader G.K. Vasan also criticised Mr. Shivakumar’s remarks on constructing the Mekedatu dam, stating his demand for the Centre’s support and his interpretation of the Supreme Court’s verdict were unacceptable.

In a statement, Mr. Vasan said Karnataka’s efforts to construct the dam amounted to an infringement of Tamil Nadu’s rights. The Mekedatu water issue was not merely a crop-related concern but a matter of survival for farmers in Tamil Nadu, he said.
Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam / Indian National Congress / Tamil Maanila Congress

articles.title: German delegation visits Auroville
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Ambassador also expressed his interest in the founders’ spiritual vision and said he planned to return to Auroville in December

German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck, accompanied by Michael Hasper, Consul General at the German Consulate General in Chennai, visited the international township of Auroville on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

The delegation was received by officials of the Auroville Foundation, including Officer on Special Duty G. Seetharaman, along with members of the Auroville Town Development Council (ATDC) and the Working Committee.

According to a press note, the centrepiece of the visit was an interactive meeting with the ATDC and the Working Committee, addressed virtually by Jayanti S. Ravi, Secretary of the Auroville Foundation (Ministry of Education, Government of India) and Additional Chief Secretary to the Government of Gujarat.

Foundation officials briefed the delegation on progress under the township’s Galaxy Master Plan, including the 98 per cent completion of the 4.4-km circular Crown Road, which links Auroville’s Residential, Industrial, Cultural and International zones, and upcoming projects such as youth housing, a Civic Anchor Town Hall, the Morning Star Women’s Wellness Center and CIRHU, the Centre for International Research on Human Unity.

They also presented Auroville’s economic life, comprising some 150 production and service units and 700 micro-enterprises, including solar energy initiatives such as Sunlit Future, the Solar Kitchen, and Svaram, its musical instrument research and production centre.

Highlighting the historical and intellectual affinities between India and Germany, particularly Germany’s tradition of Sanskrit and Vedic scholarship, Ms. Ravi proposed a roadmap for Indo-German engagement in Auroville.

The proposals include participation by German authors, poets and artists in the Auroville Literary Festival in December and events at the 12 cultural venues of Bharat Nivas, structured internships and exchange programmes linking German universities with Auroville’s youth and research units, German film screenings at Cinema Paradiso, and collaboration on sports culture and youth training.

The delegation later toured the Matrimandir and its gardens and the Amphitheatre. The Ambassador also expressed his interest in the founders’ spiritual vision and said he planned to return to Auroville in December.

German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck, accompanied by Michael Hasper, Consul General at the German Consulate General in Chennai, visited the international township of Auroville on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

The delegation was received by officials of the Auroville Foundation, including Officer on Special Duty G. Seetharaman, along with members of the Auroville Town Development Council (ATDC) and the Working Committee.

According to a press note, the centrepiece of the visit was an interactive meeting with the ATDC and the Working Committee, addressed virtually by Jayanti S. Ravi, Secretary of the Auroville Foundation (Ministry of Education, Government of India) and Additional Chief Secretary to the Government of Gujarat.

Foundation officials briefed the delegation on progress under the township’s Galaxy Master Plan, including the 98 per cent completion of the 4.4-km circular Crown Road, which links Auroville’s Residential, Industrial, Cultural and International zones, and upcoming projects such as youth housing, a Civic Anchor Town Hall, the Morning Star Women’s Wellness Center and CIRHU, the Centre for International Research on Human Unity.

They also presented Auroville’s economic life, comprising some 150 production and service units and 700 micro-enterprises, including solar energy initiatives such as Sunlit Future, the Solar Kitchen, and Svaram, its musical instrument research and production centre.

Highlighting the historical and intellectual affinities between India and Germany, particularly Germany’s tradition of Sanskrit and Vedic scholarship, Ms. Ravi proposed a roadmap for Indo-German engagement in Auroville.

The proposals include participation by German authors, poets and artists in the Auroville Literary Festival in December and events at the 12 cultural venues of Bharat Nivas, structured internships and exchange programmes linking German universities with Auroville’s youth and research units, German film screenings at Cinema Paradiso, and collaboration on sports culture and youth training.

The delegation later toured the Matrimandir and its gardens and the Amphitheatre. The Ambassador also expressed his interest in the founders’ spiritual vision and said he planned to return to Auroville in December.

articles.title: Palaniswami urges Vijay to raise Mekedatu issue with Congress leadership
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Palaniswami criticised Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar for repeatedly asserting that building a dam at Mekedatu was Karnataka’s right and required no one’s permission

AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Sunday (November 15, 2026) urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to take up Karnataka’s proposed Mekedatu dam project with the Congress leadership during his likely visit to New Delhi on Monday (November 16, 2026) and press for the implementation of Supreme Court orders on the Cauvery issue.

In a statement, Mr. Palaniswami criticised Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar for repeatedly asserting that building a dam at Mekedatu was Karnataka’s right and required no one’s permission. He said such remarks could create differences between the people of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.

Accusing the Congress government in Karnataka of disregarding the Supreme Court verdict on water release, Mr. Palaniswami said the proposed dam would threaten irrigation in the Cauvery Delta districts and drinking water supply to 20 districts in Tamil Nadu. He urged Mr. Vijay to raise the issue with Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge.

articles.title: Three arrested in Bhopal for duping Delhi woman of ₹71 lakh in ‘digital arrest’ scam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The accused impersonated an IPS officer and threatened the victim with arrest in a fake ₹6.5-crore money laundering case; IFSO uncovers a network of mule bank accounts used to route the cheated money

Three persons from Madhya Pradesh’s Bhopal have been arrested for duping a woman of ₹71 lakh by impersonating an IPS officer and threatening her with arrest in a digital arrest scam, officials from Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit of the Delhi Police said on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

The accused, identified as Priyanka Prajapati (31), Aman Soni (28) and Pinky Soni (30), were arrested from Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh by the IFSO officials. The investigation also unearthed a network of mule bank accounts used to receive and divert money obtained through cyber fraud.

According to the police, the victim received a WhatsApp video call from a person posing as an IPS officer posted in Mumbai. The caller told her that a credit card had been issued in her name and was being used for money laundering involving transactions worth approximately ₹6.5 crore.

The fraudster threatened to arrest her and send her to judicial custody, and coerced her into transferring money under the pretext of verification to avoid legal action. Under fear and intimidation, the woman transferred ₹71 lakh in two transactions, the police said.
An e-FIR was registered at the Special Cell police station on October 8, following which the IFSO unit took up the investigation.

During the probe, the police traced the financial trail and identified multiple bank accounts allegedly used to receive and divert the cheated money. The three accused were part of this network and facilitated the movement and withdrawal of the funds in coordination with other handlers.

The police said approximately ₹15 lakh was withdrawn and distributed among the accused and their associates. A portion of the cheated money was also allegedly used to purchase expensive mobile phones.
Three newly purchased mobile phones, suspected to have been bought using the defrauded money, have been recovered from the accused.
Further investigation is underway to identify the larger network involved in the fraud and tracing the proceeds of the crime.

articles.title: Mahanagar Gas hikes CNG prices in Mumbai by ₹1.5/kg, sixth hike since May
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Cumulatively prices of the vehicular gas have increased ₹9.5 per kg across six tranches since May 14
Amid rising costs of input gas, Mahanagar Gas Ltd (MGL) increased prices of compressed natural gas (CNG) at their retail outlets ₹1.5 per kg.
Effective November 15, CNG in Mumbai would be priced at ₹91.5 per kg in Mumbai.
Cumulatively prices of the vehicular gas have increased ₹9.5 per kg across six tranches since May 14.
Moreover, the latest is the second hike in the ongoing month.

The uncertainty in West Asia and the loss of supplies from Qatar, which is the world’s largest LNG producer and among the most reliable suppliers, have obligated purchasers to further alternate scouting of the natural gas and increasingly buy at spot.

In a statement, MGL said, “The ongoing Middle East crisis, coupled with reduced domestic gas allocation and increased dependence on higher-cost imported RLNG linked to international benchmarks, has significantly increased MGL’s gas procurement costs, particularly for the CNG segment, driven by strong demand and a higher share of imported gas in its input mix.”
Previously, privately-owned Adani Total Gas too have also hiked CNG prices at their outlets cumulatively by ₹6.75 per kg across two tranches since October 23.

articles.title: Indian student jailed for 30 years for online child sex abuse in U.K.
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15

A 27-year-old Indian student described by U.K. authorities as a “serial online groomer” was sentenced to 30 years’ imprisonment in north-west England on Friday (November 13, 2026) for “exploiting and coercing” several children online to commit sexual acts.

Bilal Kazi was sentenced at Chester Crown Court after pleading guilty to a series of child sexual abuse offences committed online. The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15.

“Bilal Kazi acted with absolute ruthlessness in grooming, manipulating and exploiting a large number of young vulnerable girls," said Martin McRobb, Specialist Prosecutor at the U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

“He befriended them online and forced them to take photos and videos of them carrying out sexual acts. He then blackmailed those who refused to comply with his further demands, threatening to post the explicit imagery to others.

“He posed as a teenage boy in order to attract and gain the trust of his victims and caused many to think that they were in a genuine relationship with him. When the victims realised they had been deceived, they were understandably distressed, and some suffered serious and long-term trauma," he said.
The CPS said its Organised Child Sexual Abuse Unit presented the court with overwhelming evidence gathered by police investigators in Cheshire and the West Midlands.

“The scale of Kazi’s offending meant this was a truly mammoth investigation, requiring significant resources and close collaboration across the force,” said Detective Constable Georgia Hughes, of the Online Child Abuse Investigation Team at Cheshire Constabulary.

“The girls targeted by Kazi were young and vulnerable. For many, their interactions with him were their first experience of what they believed to be a romantic relationship. Exploiting that trust, Kazi manipulated them into believing that his behaviour was normal.

“His offending has had a profound and lasting impact on the victims. Many lived in constant fear of what he would do if they failed to comply with his demands, and some have carried that fear with them for years. What should have been important formative years have instead been overshadowed by the trauma of Kazi's abuse," he said.

According to the police force, the first victim explained that she began speaking to Kazi on Snapchat when she was 13, believing him to be the same age. Their conversations quickly turned explicit in nature, with Kazi asking the victim several inappropriate questions.

articles.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Starship returned from orbit and was caught by the “chopstick arms” at SpaceX’s Starbase launch pad in Texas, in a milestone for fully reusable rockets

Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday (November 14, 2026) pulled off the first-ever “catch” of a spaceship, a technical feat showing the feasibility of fully reusable rockets that would bring affordable spaceflight one step closer to reality.

The Starship emerged from the clouds after surviving the extreme heat of re-entry into Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over SpaceX’s south Texas Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2.

The success marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems, a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible.

“That was the Holy Grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds outside Starbase broke into ecstatic cheers as the spaceship came into view, with the 1977 soft rock hit “Baby Come Back” serving as the soundtrack of the final descent on SpaceX’s official livestream.

“I really do believe this is the dawn of the space age,” said Dane Walter, 38, a spectator who came from Corpus Christi, Texas. “And truly, I consider it an equivalent moment to the Wright brothers at Kitty Hawk.”

It was the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. Until now, spaceships have been single-use items, discarded or destroyed after missions, making each launch an expensive, resource-intensive venture.
The Starship spacecraft orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Mr. Musk’s Starlink internet constellation during its 22-hour journey.

SpaceX had previously captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was more complex, because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters. “I hugged ship 42 upon its return,” Mr. Musk posted on X about the captured vessel, sharing videos taken from various angles and saying it “looks great!”

Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he said.

Analyst Kathleen Curlee, of Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology, hailed the achievement but said there was more work to be done. “What SpaceX needs is multiple repeated successes to prove the capability is ready to handle sensitive payloads and missions,” she said.

The Starship spacecraft orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Mr. Musk’s Starlink internet constellation during its 22-hour journey.

SpaceX had previously captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was more complex, because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters. “I hugged ship 42 upon its return,” Mr. Musk posted on X about the captured vessel, sharing videos taken from various angles and saying it “looks great!”

Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he said.

Analyst Kathleen Curlee, of Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology, hailed the achievement but said there was more work to be done. “What SpaceX needs is multiple repeated successes to prove the capability is ready to handle sensitive payloads and missions,” she said.

articles.title: NATO to skip a leaders' summit in Albania next year as high-level meetings are scaled back
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte played down the issue. “We are flexible with NATO summits,” he said

NATO is scaling back its high-level meetings and will not hold a leaders' summit in Albania next year as previously planned amid tension within the alliance over defence spending, Iran and the war in Ukraine.

Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that “there is not yet a common position on when the summit will happen, for sure not in 2027.” He said that “in 2028, if it will be a summit, it will be in Tirana,” Albania's capital.

NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte played down the issue. “We are flexible with NATO summits,” he told The Associated Press in an interview. “We have summits when we need them,” he said, and will hold the next one “when a necessity is there.”
Until about a decade ago, NATO held summits every two years.
It's not just about gatherings between U.S. President Donald Trump and his counterparts.

NATO Defence Ministers usually meet in October, but no talks took place last month, and none are planned for October 2027. Foreign Ministers only have one scheduled meeting next year, instead of two, under what NATO describes as a “reorganization package.”

U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have each skipped a NATO meeting or left before talks ended since they came to office. Mr. Hegseth has used defence ministerial gatherings to berate or cajole European allies and Canada.
The planned summit in Albania highlights the alliance's challenges. Albania was appointed next year's host in 2025, but its name was removed from a July summit declaration.

Some allies believe that Albania is not spending enough on defence and they were reluctant to reward the country with NATO's big event. The government in Tirana is projected to spend 2.15% of its gross domestic product on defense this year.

NATO's target is for the 32 allies to spend 3.5% of GDP on core defense by 2035, and 1.5% on defense-related infrastructure. Albania is not the worst offender among the 32 member countries. Spain, Belgium and Slovenia are faring much worse.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak remains out of control in Congo six months into response
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Ebola outbreak is the deadliest of Congo’s 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016
Six months after an Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo, the disease remains out of control and efforts to contain it are faltering.

More than 11,000 cases have been recorded, and nearly half of those infected have died, according to Government data. It is the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.

Basic containment measures, including contact tracing and isolation, remain inadequate, raising doubts about authorities' ability to halt the outbreak. Experts say there is little chance of bringing it under control within the next year.

By the time the outbreak was announced in mid-May, 43 deaths had already been recorded, suggesting the virus had circulated undetected for an extended period. It has since spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces, moving at a pace aid groups have likened to wildfire.
New hotspots continue to emerge, stretching an already strained health care system.

Community transmission remains high. According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, 80% of new cases are being detected outside health surveillance, meaning most infections have not been tracked by authorities.
Experts warn of wider spread as Ebola outbreak reaches plateau
DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases, causes 5,387 deaths
Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
One-third of deaths occur at home or elsewhere in the community, where burials and other procedures are often conducted without specialist supervision, increasing the risk of transmission.

fullParagraphs: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also warned the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign
Mr. Zelenskyy also warned the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign.
Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to the colder months, with Russian President Vladimir Putin showing no sign of backing down.

articles.title: What is ‘food is medicine’? – 2 experts explain this decades-old approach to healthcare that is taking on new life
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Access to healthy food would be considered as essential as medications for patients with chronic illness

Mountains of scientific evidence support both the negative and positive effects of our eating habits on our health . Research shows that a healthy diet can help those suffering from chronic health conditions like Type 2 diabetes , heart disease and high blood pressure .

This is where “food is medicine” comes in. Food is medicine, also known as “food as medicine” and “food prescriptions,” is a movement dedicated to providing healthy food – fruits, vegetables and sometimes healthy proteins – based on a clinician’s prescription in order to prevent, manage or treat specific clinical conditions .
Prescribing food to patients is intended to convey that food is just as important as medication for health and wellness.

As researchers whose work focuses on food access and health in rural communities, we have firsthand experience running food is medicine programs in our local area in northern Mississippi. This experience has shown us the benefits and limitations of these programs in our community.

Food is medicine programs can be delivered through curated food boxes, grocery vouchers and medically tailored meals. Most programs are collaborations between nonprofit organizations, health clinics and healthcare providers. The goal of food is medicine is to improve patient health, especially for those with chronic conditions, while reducing healthcare costs.

Increasingly, food is medicine programs have become lifelines for people with food insecurity. In 2024, more than 47 million Americans, including 7.3 million children, lived in food-insecure households – meaning they were at some point uncertain of having, or did not have, enough food for everyone in the household.

Internationally, the number of people experiencing hunger rises to roughly 673 million . Rural populations are more likely to be food insecure due to the loss of local grocery stores and distance from urban centers. Unlike a food bank, food is medicine programs provide only healthy foods, which are often curated by a dietitian, to optimize patient health.

Though food is medicine isn’t formally connected to the Make American Healthy Again movement , U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. has brought new energy and attention to the concept. In January 2026, the second Trump administration launched a campaign encouraging Americans to “ Eat Real Food .”

But the food is medicine movement actually began more than 60 years ago. One of the early providers who prescribed food as medicine was civil rights activist and multiple Nobel Peace Prize winner Dr. Jack Geiger . In the 1960s, he co-founded community health centers in South Boston and the Mississippi Delta.
When government officials chastised him for prescribing food to patients in the Delta, Geiger responded, “The last time I looked at my textbooks, the most specific therapy for malnutrition was food.”

articles.title: Diabetes linked with 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's, review finds
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred
People with diabetes could be at a 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease, compared to those living without the metabolic disorder, a review of studies has found.

Researchers, led by those from Australia's Curtin University, conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 studies. They found that if 1,000 people living with type 2 diabetes were followed for a year, an estimaated average of 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder in which memory and thought processes steadily decline with age.
Cognitive risk prevention should be integrated into diabetes care, they said.

"Individuals with T2D (type 2 diabetes) experienced approximately five AD (Alzheimer's disease) cases per 1,000 person-years and a 53 per cent higher risk of AD, supporting the rationale for integrating cognitive risk prevention into diabetes care," the authors wrote in the study published in the journal Alzheimer's Research and Therapy.

Study author Emmanuel Adewuyi, an investigator fellow at Curtin University's school of population health, said the review was important as it quantifies the relative risk and incidence of Alzheimer's in people living with type 2 diabetes.

"While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Adewuyi said.

"Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often new cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes," the author said.

Databases including MEDLINE, CINAHL and Embase were searched from for publications since inception until April 2026. Forty studies, involving 27,102,559 data points, and looking at the incidence of Alzheimer's disease among people with diabetes or link between the two disorders were analysed.

articles.title: 91% of studies in India in last 5 decades linked air pollution to health effects: Analysis
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16

An analysis of more than 180 epidemiological studies examining the health impacts of air pollution across India has found that over 91% of them reported at least one adverse health association with air pollution exposure.

These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others.

The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution.

Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas.

Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said.

Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16.

Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function.

Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.

Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."

articles.title: COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns

Exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy can lead to severe outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth and congenital abnormalities in newborns, prompting experts at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to highlight maternal health risks and call for targeted adaptation strategies.

The issue comes into focus as countries at COP31 prepare to discuss progress towards the Global Goal on Adaptation, a framework to help nations develop key adaptation measures, including those needed to address the health impacts of climate change.
However, translating growing recognition of climate-related health risks into action remains a challenge, particularly in the absence of adequate financial support.
According to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), only about one per cent of formal climate finance under its financial mechanism is currently directed towards health.
The broader issue of adaptation finance for developing nations is also expected to feature prominently in discussions in the coming days.

Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of COP31, Alan Dangour, Director of Climate and Health at the Wellcome Trust, said the foundation is seeking to highlight the evidence of heat-related impacts on pregnant women through three key areas -- elevating the issues as a risk for women, developing guidelines and preparing health systems.

“We have three key points: recognising that pregnant women are a particularly vulnerable group when it comes to climate-driven extreme heat, developing guidelines to help nurses, midwives and doctors respond to the challenges pregnant women face during heatwaves, and prepare health systems for a new world shaped by climate change, and identify the most vulnerable people so they are protected,” Dangour said.
He said pregnant women were not always recognised as a particularly vulnerable group and stressed that health systems must specifically account for their needs and risks during heatwaves.

“At the moment they are not recognised as such, and they need to be included in clinical guidelines. When it comes to data, we are keen that countries record the impacts of climate change on pregnant women and then work out how their guidelines and processes can protect them,” he said.
“That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 closes in on a light-day in interstellar space for new distance record
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: NASA is looking at another 18,000 years before the spacecraft achieves a full light-year and more than double that before it comes near another star
NASA's Voyager 1 is about to become humanity's first object to reach one light-day from Earth as it pushes ever deeper into interstellar space.
That's a mind-blowing distance of more than 26 billion kilometres for the spacecraft launched 49 years ago.

When Voyager 1 reaches that remarkable milestone on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), its radio signals will take precisely 24 hours travelling at the speed of light to reach Earth — in other words, one light-day.
NASA is looking at another 18,000 years before the spacecraft achieves a full light-year and more than double that before it comes near another star.
Project manager Suzanne Dodd sees Voyager 1 as Earth's ambassador hurtling between stars while providing a “sense of wonder” on the home front.
“It's a national treasure,” she told The Associated Press . “Really extraordinary.”

To celebrate this moment, NASA is urging people from all corners to grab their phone or a flashlight to create a wave of golden light after sunset on Tuesday (November 17), using Morse code to spell the letters V-G-R, Voyager's call sign, into the night sky.

Despite sporadic problems typical of old age, Voyager 1 and its twin Voyager 2 continue to send back science and engineering data as they zoom toward different points in space at 61,000 kph. Although launched two weeks before its sibling in 1977, Voyager 2 won't reach the one light-day mark until 2035.

Voyager 1 swept past Jupiter and Saturn to scientists' delight in 1979 and 1980, respectively, before exiting the solar system. It reached what NASA defines as interstellar space — the expansive region between star systems — in 2012. Voyager 2 visited those two planets plus Uranus and Neptune, also sending back stunning photos, before entering interstellar space in 2018.

Almost every day, the Voyagers beam back details about their never-before-explored environment: the strength and direction of the magnetic field as well as tidbits about the surrounding pressure, dust and galactic cosmic rays. They're a bit like weather satellites, according to Dodd, who's worked with the Voyagers since 1984.

articles.title: RPF personnel rescue man who fell beside moving train at Secunderabad railway station
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 53-year-old man was rescued by a Railway Protection Force (RPF) personnel after he slipped into the gap between the platform and a moving train while trying to board the Godavari Express at Secunderabad Railway Station on Saturday, November 14. His children had already boarded the train when he missed their coach and attempted to get into the next one.

D. Chandraiah, from Kotapalli in Mancherial district, was travelling with his family to Mancherial. They had come to Secunderabad for the verification of certificates related to his son’s admission. As the Godavari Express began moving out of Platform No. 1 at around 5.20 p.m., Chandraiah tried to board the train but lost his balance and fell into the gap between the platform and the moving train.

D. Naresh, an Assistant Sub-Inspector of the RPF, was on duty from 2 p.m. to 10 p.m. when he noticed the incident and immediately rushed to help. He pulled Chandraiah out of the gap and brought him safely onto the platform, averting a potentially fatal accident.
Screengrab from the video showing the ASI promptly rescuing the passenger. | Photo Credit: By Arrangement

The train, which halts at Secunderabad for two minutes, had already begun departing when the incident occurred. Chandraiah was subsequently sent to Mancherial on the next available train, the Charminar Express.
The rescue was carried out under Operation Jeevan Raksha. Senior Divisional Security Commissioner A. Naveen Kumar and Inspector B. Saraswath appreciated Naresh for his prompt action.

articles.title: In latest ‘encounter’, West Bengal police kill a man accused of shooting at a constable two days ago
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is the fifth instance of an accused killed in police firing in West Bengal, within six months of the BJP coming to power in the State; this was an “extrajudicial execution”, says civil society group

A man accused of opening fire at a police constable at Santiniketan in West Bengal 's Birbhum district on Friday (November 13, 2026) was killed in a gunfight with the law enforcers on Sunday (November 15, 2026), a senior officer said.
Ratan Sheikh was killed after he opened fire at a police team while trying to evade arrest at a brick kiln in Nanoor in the same district.
This was the fifth police encounter in West Bengal in six months since the BJP came to power in the State.

Sheikh, a history-sheeter who was absconding, allegedly shot at constable Biswajit Das, injuring him in the leg, during an arrest attempt at Laik Bazar in Santiniketan police station area on November 13.
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, while reacting to the development, asks reporters, "If someone opens fire at the police, should the police offer them sweets"

articles.title: India, Bangladesh leaderships should support temporary renewal of Ganga Water Treaty, says expert
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Full revision of the Ganga Water Treaty is not possible in the four weeks left before it expires, says Manjur Ahmed Chowdhury, former Chairman of the National River Conservation Commission of Bangladesh, but ‘having a bad treaty is better than not having any treaty at all’

There is no possibility of a fully revised India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Treaty in the mere four weeks left before the 30-year-old treaty expires, Manjur Ahmed Chowdhury, former Chairman of the National River Conservation Commission of Bangladesh said on Sunday (November 15, 2026). The current treaty could be renewed for three to five years “at the last moment”, Mr. Chowdhury said, but clearance would be needed at the highest level of political leadership for it.

“Four weeks is not sufficient for revising the old Ganga Water Treaty as river water treaties require more time to finalise. But having a bad treaty is also better than not having any treaty at all. We can at least opt for a renewal of the treaty for three to five years, if the political leaderships of both sides give the green signal,” Mr. Chowdhury said.

He cautioned Bangladesh on the upcoming agriculture season of February when, as in every year, Bangladesh’s dependence on Ganga water will increase. “Without a treaty, India will not have any commitment to release water at regular intervals and that might pose a major problem for Bangladesh’s agriculture sector, economy as well as ecology,” Mr. Chowdhury said.

The Ganga Water Treaty was signed in December 1996 by Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda of India and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina of Bangladesh. Prior to the signing of the treaty, for eight years between 1988 and 1996, Bangladesh suffered due to unpredictability in the supply of the Ganga’s water, and the treaty had ensured predictability, which helped Bangladesh, Mr. Chowdhury said.

The treaty stated that “sharing between India and Bangladesh of the Ganga waters at Farakka by ten days periods from the 1st January to the 31st May every year will be with reference to the formula at Annexure 1 of the treaty”. The Annexure 1 of the treaty had ensured that if the Farakka barrage would have 70,000 cusecs or less water, then the share of water would be 50% for both India and Bangladesh. The Annexure 1 also gave out similar division of water in Farakka for 70,000 to 75,000 cusecs, and for storage beyond 75,000 cusecs.

It would be difficult for Bangladesh to demand its share of waters of the Ganga without a legally and diplomatically binding treaty, Mr. Chowdhury said. “During the Ershad (President of Bangladesh from 1983 to 1990) years, we suffered from this lack of predictability, and reverting to that era will be a setback,” he said, adding that the Government of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had not managed Bangladesh’s foreign policy requirements effectively as river water supply was related to Dhaka’s foreign policy.

“The foreign policy of the government has become unhinged from real requirements. At the moment, there is an urgent need for agreement between the political leaderships of Bangladesh and India to ensure the Ganga Water Treaty remains on track,” Mr. Chowdhury said.

The Ganga Water Treaty should have been revised and updated taking into account the problems, including sedimentation and the changes that the river had experienced over the last three decades, Mr. Chowdhury said in his conversation with The Hindu . “These updates could not be done in the last few months because of lack of meetings, and the Joint River Commission has turned out to be quite weak in performing its duties,” he said adding, “I am still hopeful that, at least by the first week of December, the two sides will act to save the treaty. But that would have to be a dramatic development.”

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 15 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

📰 India, Bangladesh leaderships should support temporary renewal of Ganga Water Treaty, says expert

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Full revision of the Ganga Water Treaty is not possible in the four weeks left before it expires, says Manjur Ahmed Chowdhury, former Chairman of the National River Conservation Commission of Bangladesh, but ‘having a bad treaty is better than not having any treaty at all’

There is no possibility of a fully revised India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Treaty in the mere four weeks left before the 30-year-old treaty expires, Manjur Ahmed Chowdhury, former Chairman of the National River Conservation Commission of Bangladesh said on Sunday (November 15, 2026). The current treaty could be renewed for three to five years “at the last moment”, Mr. Chowdhury said, but clearance would be needed at the highest level of political leadership for it.

“Four weeks is not sufficient for revising the old Ganga Water Treaty as river water treaties require more time to finalise. But having a bad treaty is also better than not having any treaty at all. We can at least opt for a renewal of the treaty for three to five years, if the political leaderships of both sides give the green signal,” Mr. Chowdhury said.

He cautioned Bangladesh on the upcoming agriculture season of February when, as in every year, Bangladesh’s dependence on Ganga water will increase. “Without a treaty, India will not have any commitment to release water at regular intervals and that might pose a major problem for Bangladesh’s agriculture sector, economy as well as ecology,” Mr. Chowdhury said.

The Ganga Water Treaty was signed in December 1996 by Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda of India and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina of Bangladesh. Prior to the signing of the treaty, for eight years between 1988 and 1996, Bangladesh suffered due to unpredictability in the supply of the Ganga’s water, and the treaty had ensured predictability, which helped Bangladesh, Mr. Chowdhury said.

The treaty stated that “sharing between India and Bangladesh of the Ganga waters at Farakka by ten days periods from the 1st January to the 31st May every year will be with reference to the formula at Annexure 1 of the treaty”. The Annexure 1 of the treaty had ensured that if the Farakka barrage would have 70,000 cusecs or less water, then the share of water would be 50% for both India and Bangladesh. The Annexure 1 also gave out similar division of water in Farakka for 70,000 to 75,000 cusecs, and for storage beyond 75,000 cusecs.

It would be difficult for Bangladesh to demand its share of waters of the Ganga without a legally and diplomatically binding treaty, Mr. Chowdhury said. “During the Ershad (President of Bangladesh from 1983 to 1990) years, we suffered from this lack of predictability, and reverting to that era will be a setback,” he said, adding that the Government of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had not managed Bangladesh’s foreign policy requirements effectively as river water supply was related to Dhaka’s foreign policy.

“The foreign policy of the government has become unhinged from real requirements. At the moment, there is an urgent need for agreement between the political leaderships of Bangladesh and India to ensure the Ganga Water Treaty remains on track,” Mr. Chowdhury said.

The Ganga Water Treaty should have been revised and updated taking into account the problems, including sedimentation and the changes that the river had experienced over the last three decades, Mr. Chowdhury said in his conversation with The Hindu . “These updates could not be done in the last few months because of lack of meetings, and the Joint River Commission has turned out to be quite weak in performing its duties,” he said adding, “I am still hopeful that, at least by the first week of December, the two sides will act to save the treaty. But that would have to be a dramatic development.”

articles.title: Telangana government urged to clear fee reimbursement dues of pharmacy colleges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana Pharmacy Colleges Managements Association, comprising 120 private colleges and 3 government colleges, with approximately 70,000 students, has urged the government to clear the fee reimbursement dues that are meagre compared to others.

The newly elected president Pulla Ramesh Babu and general secretary Kadiyala Satish said the government’s annual fee reimbursement liability towards pharmacy institutions is only around Rs 120 to Rs 130 crore, covering approximately 70,000 students across Telangana. They requested the government to clear the final year students’ dues first.

They said pharmacy students in Telangana were being absorbed in jobs immediately due to its pharma industry here contributing nearly 50–60% of the country’s pharmaceutical production. There is also a huge scope for research and employment in the clinical sector.

Regarding fees, they said Telangana has among the lowest pharmacy education fees in the country, at ₹50,000–₹60,000 annually, compared to approximately ₹1 lakh in other states. Nearly 90% of colleges operate solely on tuition fees.

Other newly elected office bearers include A. Prabhakar Reddy, Ashok Reddy, Habeebuddin, Talla Varun, Madhusdhan Reddy, Chiranjeevi and Naveen. K. Ramdass and T. Jayapal Reddy will be the chief advisor and honorary president, respectively.

articles.title: Fascists are cowards; those who fight against them are brave: Chief Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Speaking at the MSM State conference in Kozhikode, V.D. Satheesan urges young people to join the fight against fascism and defend democracy, secularism and fundamental rights.

Stating that authoritarian rulers reminiscent of Adolf Hitler and Joseph Stalin were coming to power in several countries, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has urged people, especially youngsters, to join the fight against fascist forces, protect democracy and secularism, and defend fundamental rights.

Inaugurating the valedictory session of the State conference of the Mujahid Students Movement (MSM), the students’ wing of the Kerala Nadvathul Mujahideen (KNM), at the Kozhikode beach on Sunday (November 15), Mr. Satheesan said the world was witnessing a disturbing recurrence of developments that had marked the first half of the 20th century.

“People had believed that the fight against fascism had ended with World War II, which was followed by a strong resurgence of democracy across the world. However, authoritarianism is once again gaining ground, not just in India but in several other countries,” he said.
The Chief Minister said people joining the fight against fascism should recognise that dictators and fascists had historically been “cowards”.

Quoting German poet and playwright Bertolt Brecht, he recalled a poem in which the poet, who had been forced into exile from Nazi Germany, asks a fellow German whether fear still ruled the country. The question was not whether Hitler continued to rule Germany, but whether fear had become its ruler, Mr. Satheesan said.

“Dictators and fascists are cowards. The atrocities they commit create a sense of insecurity in their own minds. They are the cowards, while those who fight against them are the brave,” the Chief Minister said.
He urged students and young people to extend their support to the fight against fascism and join the broader struggle against such forces across the country.

Praising the KNM and its student wing, Mr. Satheesan said the MSM represented a movement with progressive ideas and a strong intellectual legacy. He said the KNM had upheld patriotism since the freedom struggle and worked towards bringing together people belonging to different sections of society.
The Chief Minister also commended the organisation for its efforts to address the educational backwardness of the Muslim community and bring it to the forefront of education.

articles.title: Lalit Modi announces he has acquired British citizenship; ‘proudly’ calls it home
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Lalit Modi announced on X that he had been naturalised as a British citizen on September 20; says United Kingdom has been my home for many years

Indian Premier League (IPL) founder Lalit Modi, who has had a number of cases and investigations against him in India, announced over the weekend that he had become a British citizen. The loss of Indian citizenship – which is automatic when one accepts the citizenship of another country – further complicates the process of extraditing Mr. Modi to India.
Mr. Modi announced on X that he had been naturalised as a British citizen on September 20.

New Delhi has repeatedly pressed the U.K. for the return of Mr. Modi, along with others such as diamond jeweller Nirav Modi and entrepreneur Vija Mallya, to India to face legal proceedings. Prime Minister Narendra Modi made requests to his (then) British counterpart Keir Starmer for the return of “economic offenders and fugitives” in July 2025, when he visited the U.K., according to a government readout of their meeting.
Mr. Lalit Modi announced his new citizenship status in person at the Oxford Union on Saturday (November 14, 2026), he said, noting that November 14 was also the birthday of King Charles III.
“Thank you to my family, friends and everyone who has been part of this journey, and to the Oxford Union for providing such a memorable occasion to share this news,” he said.
“The United Kingdom has been my home for many years,” he said.

He was accused in India of financial irregularities and money laundering, as well as violating the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), stemming from his time as the Vice President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) during the 2009-2010 period. A case against Mr. Lalit Modi under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, based on an FIR filed by the Tamil Nadu police on October 13, 2010.
A non-bailable warrant was issued against Mr. Lalit Modi in 2015 after he failed to respond to multiple summonses from the Enforcement Directorate (ED).

🇬🇧 A PROUD MOMENT. A NEW CHAPTER. Today, 14 November 2026, I had the honour of addressing the Oxford Union, where I publicly shared a very special and personal milestone. I AM PROUD TO BE A BRITISH CITIZEN. 🇬🇧 On 15 September 2026, surrounded by family and friends, I celebrated my British citizenship at a ceremony that will always hold a special place in my heart. The United Kingdom has been my home for many years. It is a country I have come to admire and appreciate deeply — its people, institutions, traditions and values. Becoming British is a privilege and a responsibility that I embrace with pride, gratitude and a genuine sense of belonging. My life's journey has been shaped by different cultures and experiences, and I look forward to continuing to contribute positively to the country I proudly call home. Thank you to my family, friends and everyone who has been part of this journey, and to the Oxford Union for providing such a memorable occasion to share this news. A new chapter, with much to look forward to. And on His Majesty King Charles III's birthday, a particularly special day to share this moment. God Save the King! 🇬🇧👑 Lalit Modi Founder IPL #BritishCitizen #OxfordUnion #UnitedKingdom #GodSaveTheKing

On February 6, 2017, the ED requested the U.K. authorities to transfer Mr. Lalit Modi to India to face justice in relation to the non-bailable warrant. It used the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT) process for this.

articles.title: Alice Huang, accused of spying on Nvidia chief, entered Taiwan eight times in 2024-25: Official
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory

The woman accused of spying for Beijing during an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday (November 12, 2026).

Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory.

Jensen Huang, chief executive of the U.S.-based chip giant Nvidia, has admitted to having an extramarital affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who U.S. officials believe was working for Chinese intelligence.

Alice Huang, who is also known as Huang Le, used a Hong Kong passport to enter Taiwan "under a standard business visitor status" and there were "no special flags" about her at the time, Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) Minister Chiu Chui-cheng told lawmakers.

Mr. Chiu made the remarks in Taiwan's Parliament in response to lawmakers' questions about Alice Huang's entries into Taiwan and a New York Times report that the United States had advised Taiwan as early as 2024 to monitor her movements.
"At least we at the Mainland Affairs Council did not receive any relevant information," Mr. Chiu said.
"If we had, we definitely would have stepped up our entry screening and border flow management."
Mr. Chiu said records show that Alice Huang visited Taiwan three times in 2024 and five times in 2025. The records do not show any entries for this year, he said.

"If we had any of the kind of critical intelligence you mentioned, leading us to believe she posed a threat to Taiwanese society, we would have definitely flagged her for heightened review," Mr. Chiu said.
"For any case where there are doubts, we intensify the level of scrutiny, and if we determine there are security concerns, there is no way we would allow her to enter the country."

articles.title: Binance hack reveals crypto's uphill battle against hackers
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Cryptocurrency exchanges present unusually attractive targets because hackers can identify wallets holding enormous sums of readily transferable digital assets ⁠and, in some cases, the employees with access

An elite North Korean hacking group’s $6.3 billion theft from Binance is renewing scrutiny of a longstanding weakness in the cryptocurrency industry: hackers may need to ‌compromise only one employee to get inside, while inconsistent security practices can allow them to turn that foothold ​into a massive theft.

The October 29 heist, described by experts as the largest cryptocurrency theft ever, unfolded in ⁠a matter of minutes after months of planning and preparation, according to Binance’s initial investigation.

Cybersecurity experts said the attack raises questions not only about how exchanges defend employees against sophisticated social engineering, but also about whether they have adequate internal controls to limit what an attacker can do once an employee’s computer or ‌credentials are compromised.

Social engineering is a well-understood threat in the industry, said Jonathan Alexander, chief technology officer of S&P Global’s OpenZeppelin, a blockchain security provider. The bigger question, he said, is why exchanges do not have stronger internal safeguards ‌and circuit breakers to prevent an attacker who breaches an engineer’s computer — like what happened at Binance — from escalating access and ‌moving ⁠assets.

Varying cybersecurity practices across the industry compound the problem, Alexander said, along with a longstanding aversion among some cryptocurrency advocates ⁠to controls they view as inconsistent with blockchain’s decentralized ethos that sometimes views things such as limits on transaction amounts and automatic reviews of patterns of spending as infringing on inherent privacy rights.

“I think that falsely, that has led some people to think that things like circuit breakers, things like more controls on the accounts, would be ​unacceptable or would be absolutely in conflict with that ‌need to avoid censorship,” Alexander said. “In my view, you can have security controls and have protections against that.”

The Binance attack is the latest in a string of major cryptocurrency hacks that have resulted in more than $22.3 billion in stolen funds since 2021, according to blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis. The scale of the losses has intensified debate over whether exchanges need more consistent standards governing access, ‌transaction controls and other defenses.

“I do expect we’ll see more clarity and standardization in the kind of cybersecurity expectations and, hopefully, requirements ​for investor protection and trust,” Alexander said. “These things show why it has to change.”

Cryptocurrency exchanges present unusually attractive targets because hackers can identify wallets holding enormous sums of readily transferable digital assets ⁠and, in some cases, the employees with access to the systems controlling them.
That has made engineers and IT workers prime targets for elaborate social-engineering operations.

articles.title: Oppo Pad Mini Review | A refreshing take on what a tablet can be
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: At a time when most tablets are getting bigger, the Pad Mini takes a different route. It is compact, remarkably light and designed for people who want a tablet they can comfortably carry around

Oppo has launched the Pad Mini in India at ₹94,999. And that is quite a price to ask for a tablet in the Indian market. However, what makes this tablet interesting is not just its hardware or premium positioning. It is the approach Oppo has taken towards its design. At a time when most tablets are getting bigger , the Pad Mini takes a different route. It is compact, remarkably light and designed for people who want a tablet they can comfortably carry around. I genuinely like this approach because portability often takes a back seat in the tablet segment. The Pad Mini also brings a matte AMOLED display, a Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 processor and an 8,000mAh battery. But can a compact tablet justify a price of ₹94,999? Let’s find out.

The first thing you notice about the Oppo Pad Mini is its size. Measuring 19.44cm in height, 13.24cm in width and just 0.55cm in thickness, the tablet feels very different from conventional tablets. It weighs approximately 279g, which makes it particularly easy to carry. You can hold it comfortably for longer periods without feeling the weight that usually comes with larger tablets. This is where Oppo’s decision to go compact makes a lot of sense.

The Lavender Purple finish adds to its appeal. It looks subtle rather than flashy and gives the tablet a distinctive identity. The flat edges keep the design clean, while the slim profile makes it feel well put together. The rear camera module sits in one corner and creates a slight protrusion. This means the tablet may wobble a little when placed on a flat surface. It is a minor design compromise, but worth mentioning.

The button placement takes some getting used to. Oppo has placed the power button and volume rocker along the top edge. The USB Type-C port sits along the bottom edge, although its slightly off-centre placement may bother those who prefer symmetrical designs. The tablet also supports face unlock, but there is no fingerprint scanner.

The Oppo Pad Mini features an 8.8-inch AMOLED display with a 2.5K resolution of 2520 × 1680 pixels. It supports an adaptive refresh rate of up to 144Hz and offers a pixel density of 344 PPI. The panel also supports 10-bit colour depth and covers 100% of the DCI-P3 colour gamut.

However, the matte finish is what makes the experience more interesting. Most tablets feature glossy displays that reflect light, particularly when you use them near windows or under bright indoor lighting. The matte treatment helps reduce reflections and makes the screen more comfortable to view under harsh lights. It also gives the display a different character when compared with conventional glossy panels.

The tab offers typical brightness of 800 nits and high-brightness mode output of up to 1,600 nits. This helps with visibility in brighter environments. The adaptive refresh rate can also scale between 60Hz and 144Hz, depending on the content. Together, these features make the Pad Mini’s display one of its strongest selling points. It is a thoughtful combination of size, resolution and screen treatment.

Under the hood, the Oppo Pad Mini runs on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 mobile platform. It pairs the processor with 8GB of LPDDR5X RAM and 256GB of UFS 4.1 storage. This is flagship-grade hardware, and it gives the tablet enough headroom for demanding applications and everyday multi-tasking. The Adreno 829 GPU also handles the graphics workload.

The compact form factor does not mean Oppo has compromised on the core hardware. The Snapdragon platform should make the tablet suitable for productivity tasks, content consumption and gaming. The 144Hz display also complements the performance package by offering smoother scrolling and animations.

On the software front, the Pad Mini runs ColorOS 16. The interface gives the tablet its own identity and is designed to work alongside the larger display. Features such as face unlock and the tablet’s connectivity options add to the everyday experience.

At a time when most tablets are getting bigger, the Pad Mini takes a different route. It is compact, remarkably light and designed for people who want a tablet they can comfortably carry around

Oppo has launched the Pad Mini in India at ₹94,999. And that is quite a price to ask for a tablet in the Indian market. However, what makes this tablet interesting is not just its hardware or premium positioning. It is the approach Oppo has taken towards its design. At a time when most tablets are getting bigger , the Pad Mini takes a different route. It is compact, remarkably light and designed for people who want a tablet they can comfortably carry around. I genuinely like this approach because portability often takes a back seat in the tablet segment. The Pad Mini also brings a matte AMOLED display, a Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 processor and an 8,000mAh battery. But can a compact tablet justify a price of ₹94,999? Let’s find out.

The first thing you notice about the Oppo Pad Mini is its size. Measuring 19.44cm in height, 13.24cm in width and just 0.55cm in thickness, the tablet feels very different from conventional tablets. It weighs approximately 279g, which makes it particularly easy to carry. You can hold it comfortably for longer periods without feeling the weight that usually comes with larger tablets. This is where Oppo’s decision to go compact makes a lot of sense.

The Lavender Purple finish adds to its appeal. It looks subtle rather than flashy and gives the tablet a distinctive identity. The flat edges keep the design clean, while the slim profile makes it feel well put together. The rear camera module sits in one corner and creates a slight protrusion. This means the tablet may wobble a little when placed on a flat surface. It is a minor design compromise, but worth mentioning.

The button placement takes some getting used to. Oppo has placed the power button and volume rocker along the top edge. The USB Type-C port sits along the bottom edge, although its slightly off-centre placement may bother those who prefer symmetrical designs. The tablet also supports face unlock, but there is no fingerprint scanner.

The Oppo Pad Mini features an 8.8-inch AMOLED display with a 2.5K resolution of 2520 × 1680 pixels. It supports an adaptive refresh rate of up to 144Hz and offers a pixel density of 344 PPI. The panel also supports 10-bit colour depth and covers 100% of the DCI-P3 colour gamut.

However, the matte finish is what makes the experience more interesting. Most tablets feature glossy displays that reflect light, particularly when you use them near windows or under bright indoor lighting. The matte treatment helps reduce reflections and makes the screen more comfortable to view under harsh lights. It also gives the display a different character when compared with conventional glossy panels.

The tab offers typical brightness of 800 nits and high-brightness mode output of up to 1,600 nits. This helps with visibility in brighter environments. The adaptive refresh rate can also scale between 60Hz and 144Hz, depending on the content. Together, these features make the Pad Mini’s display one of its strongest selling points. It is a thoughtful combination of size, resolution and screen treatment.

Under the hood, the Oppo Pad Mini runs on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 mobile platform. It pairs the processor with 8GB of LPDDR5X RAM and 256GB of UFS 4.1 storage. This is flagship-grade hardware, and it gives the tablet enough headroom for demanding applications and everyday multi-tasking. The Adreno 829 GPU also handles the graphics workload.

The compact form factor does not mean Oppo has compromised on the core hardware. The Snapdragon platform should make the tablet suitable for productivity tasks, content consumption and gaming. The 144Hz display also complements the performance package by offering smoother scrolling and animations.

fullParagraphs: Hashimoto’s can damage the thyroid gland and cause hypothyroidism. But even when treatment brings thyroid hormone levels back to normal, some patients continue to report symptoms such as fatigue, hair loss and weight changes

Rashmi Ramesh, 40, from Mumbai, has been managing Hashimoto’s thyroiditis for nearly two decades. And yet, she continues to experience hair fall and fluctuations in weight. Although she was diagnosed when she was 20, she says symptoms such as puffiness around her eyes and face, lethargy and weight gain had begun when she was about 10.

Staying fit and managing her health require constant attention to sleep, diet and exercise, she says. “It is tough to stay fit. I have to work much harder than someone who doesn’t live with Hashimoto’s.” During pregnancy, she experienced substantial weight gain and water retention, along with puffiness. Managing her condition requires constant vigilance.
